entry.title: Budget Re-Planning for Grant-Free LEO Beam-Hopping Access Under Admission Control
entry.summary: Re-Planning Budgets under Admission Control in Grant-Free LEO Beam-Hopping Access arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies how reordering visits in low-Earth-orbit beam-hopping affects grant-free update delivery when each region is served once per frame. It derives the largest allowed inter-frame position change that keeps the delivery-rate loss within a set tolerance, and identifies the exact worst-case loss. In a 40-group collision example, raising the loss tolerance from zero to 1% increases the limit from 17 to 24 positions. With independent priorities, the method keeps over 90% of the priority-weighted waiting-cost reduction of unrestricted ordering.

entry.title: Dynamics-aware compression of linear systems that keeps reduced models realizable for estimation and control.
entry.summary: Dynamics Aware Past-Future Information Bottleneck arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper notes that the standard Past-Future Information Bottleneck (PF-IB) can yield compressed linear dynamical systems that lack structural consistency and cannot be realized as dynamical systems. The authors constrain the objective to a manifold of block Hankel matrices and prove this manifold is a Lie group, linking PF-IB to realization theory. The approach is demonstrated in numerical simulations.

entry.title: Eliciting Information Through Ordinal Agreement
entry.summary: Information Elicitation by Ordinal Agreement arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper proposes a simple ordinal peer-prediction mechanism that rewards agents for pairwise agreement, measured by Kendall tau, so they truthfully compress private information into coarser ordinal reports. Under a broad class of Bayesian Stochastically Order Consistent models, including Mallows and Thurstone, the authors prove truthful reporting is stochastically dominant and strongly truthful under index-equivariant strategies. Experiments on synthetic Mallows and Thurstone data and the SUSHI preference dataset show truthful payments shifted rightward and the highest normalized sensitivity among tested baselines. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose a Kendall-tau pairwise-agreement ordinal peer-prediction mechanism, prove stochastic dominance of truthful reporting, and report experiments on synthetic and SUSHI data.

entry.title: Perfect hashing's probabilistic bound is tight only for binary alphabets
entry.summary: The probabilistic bound for perfect hashing is sharp only for binary alphabets arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies the optimal asymptotic rate R_q of perfect q-hash codes, a basic extremal problem in combinatorics, information theory, and computer science. The authors prove that R_q equals the classical probabilistic lower bound B_q if and only if q=2, so strict improvements exist for every q≥3, partly settling a conjecture of Xing and Yuan. For sufficiently large q they show an improvement of order exp(-(2+η)q) over B_q, and they establish that concatenation methods need exponentially long inner codes to reach this scale.

entry.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
entry.summary: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper determines the maximum number of common zeros in projective space for any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the size of the finite field. This proves a conjecture of Beelen, Datta and Ghorpade and yields the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof combines Green's hyperplane restriction bound with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. ★★★★ Notable: The authors determine the maximum common zeros of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials, proving a conjecture and the full weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes.

entry.title: NOMA-Assisted Coordinated Beam Hopping for VLEO Satellite Networks
entry.summary: NOMA Assisted Coordinated Beam Hopping for VLEO Satellite Communication Systems arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper studies a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) assisted coordinated beam hopping scheme for very low Earth orbit (VLEO) satellite systems, where multiple satellites jointly serve ground users and a ground station. The authors model the channel with atmospheric attenuation, Doppler effects, and pointing perturbations, and propose a low-complexity decoupled algorithm for beam scheduling and power allocation. Simulations show higher sum rate, lower outage probability, and greater delivered traffic than orthogonal multiple access benchmarks.

entry.title: Uniform three-fold product expansion of algebraic-geometry codes over one fixed field
entry.summary: Uniform Three-Fold Product Expansion of Algebraic-Geometry Codes over a Fixed Field arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper studies product expansion for classical codes, where low-weight words decompose into sums of words supported on few lines. The authors show that one-point evaluation codes on the Garcia–Stichtenoth tower over F_729 have three-fold product expansion with a constant independent of length. This yields an explicit fixed-field family whose dual codes have rate tending to 109/130 and relative distance at least 8/65. The proof is geometric and relies on an exact generation theorem and a support-localisation argument. ★★★★ Notable: The authors construct the first explicit fixed-field family with constant rate, linear distance, and three-fold product expansion, via a geometric proof reportedly formally verified in Lean 4.

entry.title: Drift-resilient interference prediction: online adaptation of an extreme-value predictor
entry.summary: Drift-Resilient Predictive Interference Management: Online Adaptation of an Extreme-Value Predictor arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper addresses ultra-reliable low-latency communication, where interference must be predicted and resources allocated against its high conditional quantile. It proposes event-triggered adaptation for an extreme-value/kernel-density predictor: a CUSUM test detects distribution changes, after which the quantile partition is re-derived and each state is refit from bounded memory. Across several drift scenarios, it reports lower channel use and pinball loss than cumulative refitting at similar coverage, with predictor memory bounded rather than growing over time.

entry.title: Balancing redundancy and synergy in partial information decomposition
entry.summary: Between Hi-Fi and MMI: the overlap of redundancy and synergy in partial information decomposition arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies partial information decomposition (PID), which splits the information two sources carry about a target into redundant, unique, and synergistic parts. The authors parameterize the feasible segment by an overlap quantity and show that many named PID redundancy measures can be written as the largest positive part of co-information over a set of reference distributions, which orders these measures along the segment. The paper also extends the analysis to three or more sources and finds that zero overlap on all pairs at once often cannot be achieved.

entry.title: GUARDTs: Decentralized Access Control for Replicated Data Types
entry.summary: GUARDTs: Decentralized Access Control for Replicated Data Types arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents GUARDTs (Guarded Unforgeable Algebraic Replicated Data Types), which embed fine-grained permissions directly into the application data model. The approach operates without a central authority, supports dynamic policy evolution, and tolerates Byzantine replicas. The authors formally prove that GUARDTs guarantee confidentiality, integrity, and availability. Experiments show that the access control adds negligible overhead beyond the cost of Byzantine-resilient replication.

entry.title: Quantum Advantage in Certifying Graph Properties with Smaller Certificates
entry.summary: Quantum Advantage in Local Certification of Graph Properties arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies local certification, where network nodes verify global properties using certificates from an untrusted prover and communication with neighbors, with complexity measured by the maximum certificate size. Working in the distributed quantum Merlin-Arthur (dQMA) model, the authors establish unconditional exponential and polynomial quantum advantages for graph properties depending only on network topology, with complexity measured in the number of vertices n. They give a one-round dQMA protocol with O(μ log n)-qubit certificates for a fixed μ, whereas any μ-round distributed Merlin-Arthur protocol needs Ω(n/(μ log²n))-bit certificates. For graph symmetry, they present a one-round dQMA protocol with Õ(n^{5/3})-qubit certificates, improving on the known Ω(n²)-bit lower bound for one-round dMA protocols. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove unconditional exponential and polynomial quantum advantages for graph property local certification, resolving an open question of Hasegawa et al.

entry.title: xDSL-CCPP: A new code generator for atmospheric models
entry.summary: xDSL-CCPP: An alternative code generator for atmospheric modelling arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The Common Community Physics Package (CCPP) helps exchange physics packages between atmospheric models, and its core is a Python code generator that turns specifications into Fortran. This paper presents xDSL-CCPP, a replacement generator built on the MLIR and xDSL compiler frameworks. The authors report that the bespoke tooling shrank from about 15,000 to 5,000 lines of code. They argue these frameworks lower the barrier to building application-specific domain specific languages for high performance computing while keeping performance.

entry.title: Memory-Bounded Inference for a 22B Audio-Video Generator
entry.summary: Precision - Preserving Subtensor Inference for a 22B Joint Audio - Video Generator under a Fixed GPU Working Set arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents PSI, a fixed-arena runtime that runs the BF16 LTX-2.5 22B joint audio-video transformer by streaming sub-block weights and managing intermediate state separately. On an RTX A6000 across nine matched prompts, sampled transformer-process peak memory drops from 8,578 MiB to 360 MiB, while mean transformer time rises from 247.11 s to 349.00 s. The authors also report that mean endpoint error increases across the nine full-prompt cases.

entry.title: Operational Indirect Rate-Distortion Functions for Classification
entry.summary: Operational Indirect Rate-Distortion Functions for Classification Tasks arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies indirect source coding for classification, where the encoder only observes a source Z while the decoder must reconstruct a semantic source X. The authors attribute the gap between theoretical indirect rate-distortion limits and learned coding schemes such as VIB and VAE to the latent representation, the DNN architecture and training loss, and whether the encoder is task-aware. They introduce four operational rate-distortion functions that account for these factors and establish a hierarchy among them. These functions are derived for a Gaussian mixture source, and numerical results on Gaussian mixtures and CIFAR-100 quantify the rate loss from each effect.

entry.title: Modular Model Checking for Threshold-Based Distributed Algorithms
entry.summary: Modular Parameterized Model Checking of Threshold-Based Distributed Algorithms arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a method for checking fault-tolerant distributed algorithms by splitting them into modules, verifying each one separately, and replacing them with a synchronous abstraction. The authors introduce a new system model combining aspects of threshold automata and global synchronization protocols, and study its expressiveness. They provide a bounded model checking procedure and a way to check the correctness of the abstraction step, and report promising experimental results on a case study.

entry.title: Quantum Communication and Phase Sensing Over a Noisy Dephasing Channel
entry.summary: Quantum Communication and Phase Sensing over a Dephasing Channel with Thermal Noise arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies transmission of coherent states over a von Mises dephasing channel with thermal noise, using a heterodyne receiver. The authors derive the symbol-error probability and a closed-form approximation, revealing an irreducible error floor caused by dephasing. They also provide closed-form bounds on the Fisher information and quantum Fisher information for estimating the channel's mean phase. The work examines when communication reliability and phase-estimation requirements can be met jointly.

entry.title: Over-the-Scene Computation: Using Designed Radar Illumination to Estimate Crowds Without Resolving Individuals
entry.summary: Over-the-Scene Computation: Illumination-Programmed Functional Sensing of Unresolvable Populations arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes over-the-scene computation, in which the illumination waveform makes the scene itself perform calculations, so unresolved members of a population need not be individually detected. The waveform's ambiguity function is treated as the transfer function that determines which functionals can be computed and their noise cost. For a chirp, the authors report estimates within 16% of the Cramér-Rao bound at a specified SNR and member density, using 77 times fewer samples than the compared unbiased estimators.

entry.title: Distributed nonsmooth optimization with general constraints: a unified algorithm and convergence analysis
entry.summary: Distributed Optimization Involving Non-Lipschitzian, Linear Composite Functions: Unified Algorithm Design and Convergence Analysis arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies a general distributed nonsmooth optimization problem over networked multi-agent systems, with edge-based equality constraints, local convex inequality constraints, and global affine and nonlinear coupling constraints. The goal is to minimize the sum of local nondifferentiable convex functions and proximable nonsmooth composite terms tied to linear operators. The authors derive a new local first-order condition and propose a fully distributed algorithm based on variable decomposition and proximal operators, using locally fixed step-sizes. Under mild assumptions, it achieves an o(1/k) convergence rate, and numerical experiments support the theory.

entry.title: A Universal Threshold Theory for Local Properties of Random Linear Codes
entry.summary: A Universal Threshold Theory for Local Properties of Random Linear Codes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the threshold at which random linear codes satisfy local properties, which are monotone properties that a small set of codewords can witness. It shows the threshold lies within O(b) dimensions of the expectation threshold for b-local properties. This yields a derandomization result: decreasing local properties that hold for random linear codes at a given rate also hold at similar rates for pseudorandom ensembles, including codes with small-bias parity-check matrices. Applications include maximum loads in linear hashing, rank-metric list decoding, and list decoding under insertion-deletion and burst errors. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors show the threshold of a b-local property for random linear codes lies within O(b) dimensions of the expectation threshold, yielding a general derandomization that extends to linear hashing

entry.title: Optimizing beamforming, antenna positions, and task buffering for energy-efficient mobile edge computing
entry.summary: Joint Flexible Beamforming, Resource Allocation, and Task Buffering for Movable-Antenna Enabled MEC Systems arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a mobile edge computing framework that uses movable antennas and task buffering to handle bursty workloads and changing channels. Antennas can be repositioned continuously to improve array gain, and buffer queues separate task generation from execution, enabling multi-slot scheduling. The authors minimize long-term energy consumption by jointly optimizing receive beamforming, antenna positions, and computing resources, using Lyapunov optimization and an alternating optimization algorithm. Simulations show the scheme significantly reduces energy consumption compared with benchmarks while keeping task queues stable under unpredictable traffic.

entry.title: Limits of list-decoding Reed-Solomon codes: some restrictions in recent work are unavoidable.
entry.summary: Combinatorial limitations of list-decoding Reed-Solomon codes arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper shows that for infinitely many rates, full-length Reed-Solomon codes over low-characteristic fields can contain super-polynomially many codewords in a Hamming ball slightly larger than the Johnson radius. Over prime fields, it constructs full-length Reed-Solomon codes of constant rate with polynomially many codewords in a Hamming ball of relative radius strictly below 1-R. This disproves a recent conjecture that list sizes below capacity are always constant over prime fields. ★★★★ Notable: The authors refute a conjecture bounding list sizes over prime fields and give super-polynomial codeword constructions over low-characteristic fields.

entry.title: Cores of 3-distant convex games: a study of stable profit-sharing in cooperative games that only break convexity between closely related groups.
entry.summary: Cores of 3-distant convex games arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the core of 3-distant convex cooperative games, which allow convexity to be violated only between closely related coalitions. The authors give a simple necessary and sufficient condition for the core to be nonempty. They also present a strongly polynomial-time combinatorial algorithm that finds a core allocation whenever one exists. The framework is applied to oligopolistic competition with merger synergies and to profit allocation in joint production with complementary inputs.

entry.title: Measuring CUDA Locality Domains on Blackwell GPUs
entry.summary: Characterizing CUDA Locality Domains on Blackwell GPUs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This report evaluates the Locality Domain (LD) feature introduced in CUDA 13.4 on a node with eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs. It examines latency sources in memory access, computation, and communication, and how LD can mitigate them. Die-aware adaptations yield speedups of up to 43.5% for NCCL AllGather, 111.3% for nvbandwidth DtoD, and 37% for DeepGEMM. The authors also identify LD-related allocation overhead above 32 MB and propose a GPU driver fix that reduces it 7x to 10x without user-code changes.

entry.title: Transparency in Team Contracts: Joint Design of Information Disclosure and Incentive Contracts
entry.summary: Transparency in Team Contracts arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies how a principal, who knows more about a project's success chances than the agents, can combine team contracts that share rewards with information disclosure (Bayesian persuasion) to incentivize effort. It shows that full transparency achieves a tight 4/3-approximation to the optimal combination when the production function is submodular, but can be arbitrarily suboptimal when it is supermodular. The authors also present a deterministic polynomial-time approximation algorithm for pure multi-agent contract design. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show full transparency achieves a tight 4/3-approximation for submodular production, and improve pure multi-agent contract approximation to 2.311.

entry.title: Polynomial-time approximate EFX allocation of chores via flow and matching
entry.summary: Polynomial-Time Approximate EFX for Chores via Flow and Matching arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies approximate EFX allocations of indivisible chores under nonnegative additive costs. The authors present a polynomial-time algorithm that computes a complete (3+ε)-EFX allocation for any rational 0<ε≤1, reducing the earlier agent-dependent factor to a constant. The method extends to EFkX with a (2+1/k+ε)-approximation for every integer k≥1. For instances with few chores, the BRBI algorithm gives stronger guarantees, including exact EFkX when m≤2kn. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve approximate EFX chore allocation from an agent-dependent factor to constant 3+ε, with new tightness and lower-bound results.

entry.title: RARE: A new equilibrium for pricing games where sellers can respond to price changes
entry.summary: RARE: Response-Aware Rational Equilibrium in Budget-Constrained Pricing Games arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies pricing games in markets where budget-constrained buyers choose utility-maximizing bundles and each seller sets a price for one good. It proposes Response-Aware Rational Equilibrium (RARE), in which any seller's deviation can be deterred by other sellers' responses, and shows that RARE exists under certain conditions, with approximate versions for some cases. The authors also analyze a price-raising dynamic that reaches an approximate RARE.

entry.title: Existence of Two-Sided Product Expanding Codes Using Rademacher Matrices
entry.summary: Product Expansion of Random Codes via Analytic Techniques arXiv · Oct 2, 2026The paper proves that two-sided product expanding codes exist without relying on explicit constructions of asymptotically optimal locally testable codes (c³-LTCs), unlike an earlier result by Kalachev and Panteleev. It shows that independent random linear codes over a sufficiently large prime field have constant two-sided product expansion with probability tending to one, for fixed numbers of component codes with rates bounded away from zero and one. The trade-off is that the field characteristic must grow with the block length, whereas the earlier work used extensions of F₂. ★★★★ Notable: The authors replace explicit c^3-LTC constructions with random Rademacher matrices over the reals and use the trace power method to show two-sided product expanding codes exist; they report random lin

entry.title: Speech-enhancement-based deep semantic autoencoder design for wireless communication
entry.summary: Design of a Speech Enhancement-Based Deep Semantic Autoencoder for Wireless Communications arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a Speech enhancement-based Deep Semantic Autoencoder (S-DSA) system for transmitting speech over wireless channels. It combines a dual-branch semantic encoder, channel encoder and decoder, and two semantic decoders to perform joint source-channel coding. Its core is an adaptive semantic noise decoupling mechanism that separates target speech semantics from noise representations, keeping semantics consistent at low SNR. The authors report better speech-noise separation, higher robustness, and improved reconstruction quality.

entry.title: Energy-time optimal decoding using expander-graph LDPC codes on mesh networks
entry.summary: Energy-Time Optimal Decoding Using Expander-Graph LDPC Codes and Mesh Network Architecture arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper constructs the first decoding schemes within the Thompson VLSI model that are energy optimal up to polylogarithmic factors and also reach clock cycle lower bounds. The approach combines expander-graph-based LDPC codes, a mesh network architecture, and a parallelization technique. A key graph-theory lemma shows that bounded-degree communication graphs can be routed through two- and three-dimensional meshes without overflowing any node's memory.

entry.title: Functional Converses for Private Matrix-Product Retrieval Under Correlated Server Libraries
entry.summary: Functional Converses for Private Matrix-Product Retrieval under Library-Wide Decoder-Side Correlation arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies private retrieval of the matrix product A^T B from replicated servers, where B equals A plus independent noise and the servers store a library correlated with A. The authors measure only additional leakage and require index privacy conditioned on A. For A of rank below m, they prove a lower bound on the retrieval cost in terms of the replicated colluding private-information-retrieval capacity. In the full-rank case the bound becomes tight.

entry.title: Not All Loops Cost the Same: Phase-dependent loop depth for serving looped transformers
entry.summary: Not All Loops Cost the Same: Phase-Dependent Depth for Serving Looped Transformers arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents LoopDuet, a training-free serving method that chooses separate loop depths for the prefilling and decoding phases of looped transformers. It is implemented in vLLM by gathering tokens that need further recurrence into compact batches, so the chosen allocation yields real savings. Experiments on HotpotQA show that separate phase budgets improve the quality-throughput trade-off and that adaptive prefilling retains more quality under load.

entry.title: From ISA to Shared Execution: Capability Gain on AMD MI300A and MI250X
entry.summary: Capability Gain from ISA to Shared Execution on AMD MI300A and MI250X arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper compares AMD's MI300A (CDNA3) with its predecessor MI250X (CDNA2) and introduces "capability gain," a metric for how much of an instruction-level speedup survives at higher levels such as libraries, applications, or shared devices. It traces the measurements from ISA microbenchmarks through hipBLASLt, hipSPARSELt, LLM inference, and mixed-precision HPL, including a device shared by up to eight concurrent streams. Results show FP8 keeps most of its speedup through the library, while unfused quantization causes per-layer slowdown in an LLM, and 2:4 sparsity keeps at most about half its speedup in hipSPARSELt.

entry.title: Lossless source coding that forces each symbol's marginal distribution to match a target exactly.
entry.summary: Lossless Source Coding with Marginal Distribution Constraint arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies lossless source coding where encoded symbols must each have a marginal distribution exactly equal to a target distribution. Unlike distribution matching methods that only require approximate i.i.d. behavior, this imposes a strict per-symbol constraint. The authors derive nonasymptotic lower and upper bounds on the optimal encoding length. They exactly characterize the first-order coding rate when the source or target distribution is uniform, or when the source is i.i.d.

entry.title: Preemption Based on Elapsed Service Time to Minimize Age of Information
entry.summary: Elapsed-Service-Time-Aware Preemption for Age of Information Minimization arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper studies age of information and peak age of information in a status update system where several independent sources share one server with generally distributed service times. It proposes a self-preemptive policy in which an in-service update is preempted with a probability depending on its elapsed service time, and develops a unified analysis using non-homogeneous absorbing continuous-time Markov chains and semi-Markov chains. Numerical results show that preemption benefits depend on the hazard-rate structure of service times, and in a dual-source lognormal setting, jointly tuned threshold-based preemption yields lower sum average age of information than age-independent policies.

entry.title: NUMA-Torch: Compiler-driven NUMA-aware LLM prefill on multi-socket CPUs
entry.summary: NUMA-Torch: Compiler-Driven NUMA-Aware LLM Prefill on Multi-Socket CPUs arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper addresses slow prefill of large language models on multi-socket CPUs, where memory bandwidth rather than compute is the bottleneck. It modifies the TorchInductor compiler to be NUMA-aware, using NUMA-aware tensor parallelism that shards weights across sockets and keeps threads and memory allocations local via CPU affinity. Evaluated on GPT-2, BERT and Gemma 3 270M across several Haswell and Cascade Lake platforms, the approach reduces cross-socket traffic and achieves prefill speedups of up to 2.63x.

entry.title: DMuon: Scaling Matrix Optimizers in Data Parallelism with Topology-Aware Matrix Ownership
entry.summary: DMuon: Scaling Matrix Optimizers in Data Parallelism with Topology-Aware Matrix Ownership and Communication arXiv · Nov 5, 2026Matrix optimizers such as Muon update whole weight matrices, which clashes with the element- or row-wise sharding used by data-parallel training systems. DMuon is a matrix-granular optimizer runtime for PyTorch FSDP and HSDP that assigns each matrix a unique owner, which runs the Newton–Schulz iteration and update on the full matrix, with load balanced by computational cost. On up to 256 H100 GPUs across three dense LLMs and two VLA models, DMuon matches or exceeds the training throughput of FSDP2 with AdamW, reaching 1.05 times that at the median. Compared with a gather-then-replicate Muon baseline, its median throughput is 2.1 times higher.

entry.title: Logically Augmented Quantum LDPC Codes with Hierarchical Decoding
entry.summary: Logically Augmented Quantum LDPC Codes: Construction and Hierarchical Decoding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper proposes a joint framework for constructing and decoding logically augmented quantum LDPC codes. An auxiliary logical protection code adds extra stabilizer constraints to selected logical qubits of a primary code. A hierarchical logical list decoder, invoked only when standard belief propagation fails, selects the lowest-weight syndrome-consistent correction from hypothesis-conditioned BP runs. Numerical results show that varying the repetition length of the protection code offers a tunable rate-performance trade-off.

entry.title: Improved Randomized Online Matching Beyond 0.55 Competitive Ratio
entry.summary: Online Edge-Weighted Matching Beyond 0.55 arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper presents a randomized algorithm for edge-weighted online bipartite matching with free disposal, achieving a competitive ratio of 0.556195. This improves on the previous 0.5368 guarantee by Blanc and Charikar. The algorithm builds on online correlated selection and is analyzed with a state-dependent primal-dual method, with some selection inequalities verified by a computer-assisted proof whose verifiers are publicly available. The authors also show that triangular unit-weight inputs asymptotically attain the guarantee of the underlying ideal algorithm, indicating the analysis is tight. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the competitive ratio for edge-weighted online bipartite matching to 0.556 via state-dependent primal-dual analysis with computer-assisted verification and a tight bound.

entry.title: Prophet Secretary for Matroids and XOS Valuations: A Strict Separation at 1-1/e
entry.summary: Prophet Secretary for Matroids and XOS Valuations: A Strict Separation at 1-1/e arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies online allocation where element values are drawn independently and revealed in random order, with the goal of choosing an independent set or disjoint buyer bundles compared against the expected offline optimum. For matroids, the authors give a randomized algorithm achieving a (1-1/e+10^-6) competitive ratio with polynomial running time in the independence-oracle model. For combinatorial auctions with XOS valuations, they show 1-1/e is the optimal competitive ratio, establishing a strict separation between the two settings. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show matroid prophet-secretary beats 1-1/e and give a tight 1-1/e bound for XOS auctions, a notable separation result.

entry.title: Tight bounds for fractional and randomized truthful scheduling
entry.summary: Tight bounds for fractional and randomized truthful scheduling arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies truthful scheduling on unrelated machines and proves that every deterministic truthful fractional mechanism has worst-case approximation ratio at least (n+1)/2, matching the known upper bound. Because truthful-in-expectation mechanisms induce truthful fractional mechanisms, the same lower bound extends to all truthful-in-expectation and universally truthful mechanisms. The authors also give a universally truthful mechanism with approximation ratio n/2+o(n). Together, the results establish that the optimal leading constant for randomized truthful scheduling is 1/2. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve a longstanding open problem, proving a (n+1)/2 lower bound for truthful fractional scheduling and matching randomized upper bounds asymptotically.

entry.title: Proves that computing competitive equilibrium for linear chores is CLS-complete
entry.summary: Competitive Equilibrium for Linear Chores is CLS-complete arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the computational complexity of finding an exact competitive equilibrium in Fisher markets with divisible chores and linear disutilities. Linear goods markets admit strongly polynomial-time algorithms, but no polynomial-time algorithm was known for linear chores. The authors prove the problem is CLS-hard and therefore CLS-complete, which they claim is the first such result for a market equilibrium problem. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show computing exact CE for linear chores is CLS-complete, via reduction from KKT points of a quadratic program.

entry.title: On the Existence and Complexity of Quasi-strict Equilibria
entry.summary: On Existence and Computational Complexity of Quasi-strict Equilibria arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Quasi-strict Nash equilibrium, introduced by Harsanyi in 1973, requires every pure best response to be played with positive probability. The paper gives a simpler proof that every bimatrix game has such an equilibrium, avoiding a complicated limit argument in Norde's original proof. This proof settles the complexity of computing one by showing the problem is in PPAD. For games with three or more players, the paper shows that deciding whether a quasi-strict equilibrium exists is ∃R-complete, strengthening an earlier NP-hardness result. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a simpler existence proof, resolve PPAD membership for computing quasi-strict equilibria, and show existence deciding for three or more players is ∃R-complete.

entry.title: Exact memory-rate tradeoff for three-user secure coded caching
entry.summary: The Exact Memory-Rate Tradeoff for Three-User Secure Coded Caching arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper determines the exact zero-error memory-rate tradeoff for secure coded caching with three users and any number N≥2 of independent files. Each user recovers its requested file, while its cache and the broadcast jointly reveal no information about the complete tuple of unrequested files. For N≥4, two converse bounds confirm the optimality of known achievable points and the memory-sharing segments between them. For N=3, two additional bounds identify a new corner point at (M,R)=(3/2,2), and an explicit linear code over F_3 achieves it, lowering the rate by one quarter of a file compared with memory sharing. ★★★★ Notable: The authors exactly characterize the three-user secure caching tradeoff, identify a new corner at (3/2,2), and give an explicit F_3 linear code achieving it.

entry.title: Simulating word-RAM programs efficiently with stable population protocols
entry.summary: Efficient Stable Word-RAM Simulation by Population Protocols arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies population protocols, in which indistinguishable agents interact in random pairs, and shows how they can simulate word-RAM programs efficiently. For every polynomial-size word-RAM program, the construction is stable and silent, with stabilisation in polylogarithmic time both in expectation and with high probability. The framework supports multiple outputs, showing that efficient stable protocols compute beyond semilinear predicates. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a stable, silent, efficient population protocol simulating polynomial word-RAM programs, beyond semilinear predicates, with polylogarithmic stabilisation time in expectation and w.h.p

entry.title: One Strategic Woman: Sharp Ranks and a Persistent Core
entry.summary: One Strategic Woman: Sharp Ranks and a Persistent Core arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies a balanced random stable-marriage market in which one fixed woman misreports preferences in men-proposing deferred acceptance to secure her best attainable partner. The authors prove that her expected average true partner rank is asymptotic to (ln n)^2, improving the previous O((ln n)^4) bound, while the men's average rank is asymptotic to n/(2ln n). After normalization, the two average ranks converge jointly in distribution to (U, U^{-1}), where U is uniform on (0,1). ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the expected rank bound for one manipulating woman in stable matching and give joint distributional convergence results.

entry.title: Two-sided screening: how platforms design quality, price and wage menus in differentiated markets
entry.summary: Two-Sided Screening in Quality-Differentiated Markets arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Motivated by platforms such as Uber and Airbnb, this paper studies how a two-sided platform designs a menu of qualities, consumer prices and provider wages when both sides self-select based on private values and costs. The authors characterize profit- and welfare-optimal trading distributions and show that production technology alone can reduce menu size without losing optimal profit or welfare. They also prove that under monotone hazard rate conditions a profit-optimal menu achieves at least 1/(e-1) of optimal welfare, and they give a polynomial-time algorithm for restricted menu sizes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors combine two-sided screening with quality menu design, characterize optimal trading distributions via convexification, and report a 1/(e-1) welfare approximation for profit-optimal menus.

entry.title: Constant-round parallel algorithms for approximate minimum spanning trees in metric spaces
entry.summary: Constant-Round Massively Parallel Algorithms for Approximate MSTs in Metric Spaces arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a unified framework for computing approximate minimum spanning trees in metric spaces under the fully scalable Massively Parallel Computation (MPC) model. It gives results for general metrics, Euclidean spaces, and doubling metrics, specifying the approximation ratio, number of rounds, and space usage for each. For general metrics, the round complexity is asymptotically optimal in its dependence on the error parameter, and the work answers an open question from STOC'23. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a unified framework yielding constant-round MPC approximate MSTs, with a round bound matching a stated lower bound in epsilon.

entry.title: Breaking the One-Player Extension Barrier: History-Aware Repair for Multiplayer Approximate Nash Equilibria
entry.summary: Breaking the One-Player Extension Barrier: History-Aware Repair for Multiplayer Approximate Nash Equilibria arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies polynomial-time algorithms for approximate Nash equilibria in multiplayer games, where prior methods relying on one-player extension could only improve the classical 1-1/m guarantee to 1-1/(m-c). The authors propose an iterative descent-and-repair framework that directly handles general m-player games and achieves a 1-(σ⋆-ε)/m approximation for sufficiently large m, where σ⋆ ≈ 1.5867. A new potential function inspired by continuous-time dynamics certifies progress across iterations and ensures polynomial-time termination. ★★★★ Notable: The authors break the long-standing one-player extension barrier for multiplayer approximate Nash equilibria via a history-aware iterative repair framework, with polynomial-time termination proved for

entry.title: Complete Characterization of q-Ary 2-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes
entry.summary: A Complete Characterization of q-Ary 2-Designs in Doubly-Extended Reed-Solomon Codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies when codewords of a fixed weight in doubly-extended Reed-Solomon codes form q-ary 2-designs. It gives an exact criterion: the number of r-subsets of nonzero field elements with a given product is independent of that product if and only if gcd(r, q-1)=1. Applying this to minimum-weight codewords, the authors show they form a q-ary 2-design exactly when gcd(k-1, q-1)=1. They also show that for MDS codes this property at minimum weight extends to all nonzero weights. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a complete characterization of q-ary 2-designs in doubly-extended Reed-Solomon codes via an exact product-counting criterion over F_q^*.

entry.title: Functional inequalities derived from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation
entry.summary: Functional inequalities from the fundamental limits of Bayesian estimation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a Bayesian information-theoretic framework for proving functional inequalities for log-concave measures. It shows that Φ-Sobolev inequalities are equivalent to lower bounds on Bayes risk for estimating functions of a variable observed through Gaussian noise. This yields a simple proof of the O(n^{1/2}) Poincaré constant bound and an improved log-Sobolev bound for subgaussian measures. The authors also recast the shared structure of three recent proofs of the Kannan–Lovász–Simonovits conjecture using low-degree MMSE tools. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish an equivalence between Φ-Sobolev inequalities and Bayesian estimation lower bounds, reporting an improved log-Sobolev constant bound of n^{1/4}.

entry.title: A mechanism for one-sided matching that keeps total travel distance low using only ranked preferences, with a new sublinear distortion bound.
entry.summary: Sublinear Metric Distortion for Matching arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies metric distortion in one-sided matching, where n agents are matched to n items in an unknown metric space and the mechanism sees only each agent's ranking of items by distance. The authors give a mechanism with distortion O(n^{log_4 3}), the first sublinear bound, improving on the O(n) guarantee of Random Serial Dictatorship. Their approach builds a partial matching from truncated Random Serial Dictatorship or Probabilistic Serial, then completes it with a new general cluster completion algorithm. The paper also tightens the distortion bounds for those two rules and improves lower bounds for truthful mechanisms. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give the first sublinear distortion bound, O(n^{log_4 3}), for one-sided matching, improving the long-standing O(n) bound via truncated mechanisms and cluster completion.

entry.title: A paper on which noisy Boolean function is most informative about a hidden bit string
entry.summary: On the most informative Boolean function under noise arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies a problem in information theory: a uniform random bit string X is passed through a channel that flips each bit independently with probability p, producing Y, and a random bit C is computed from Y. The authors prove that the mutual information between C and X is at most that between the first bit of Y and X, for all p in [0,1]. This settles a conjecture posed by Courtade and Kumar in 2013. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve the 2013 Courtade-Kumar conjecture, showing the mutual information bound holds for all flip probabilities.

entry.title: Stability and Perfection in Constrained Weighted Network Games: Defining and proving existence of stable networks, and their refinements, when agents face capacity and budget limits.
entry.summary: Stability and Perfection in Constrained Weighted Network Games arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper introduces a framework for constrained weighted network formation, where agents assign continuous weights to coalitions subject to coalitional capacity and individual budget constraints. It defines a new stability notion, coalitionwise stability, and proves that such stable networks exist under continuity and componentwise quasiconcavity of payoffs. The authors also study perfection-based refinements inspired by Selten and Bich and Teteryatnikova, and show that trembling-hand and perturbative formulations are equivalent under a componentwise monotonicity assumption.

entry.title: flash-comm: A communication library that synchronizes data transfers themselves to speed up LLM decoding.
entry.summary: flash-comm: Self-Synchronizing Collective Communication for LLM Decoding arXiv · Nov 5, 2026The paper presents flash-comm, a communication library for LLM decoding that merges readiness synchronization with data movement. Each data block carries evidence of its own readiness, so receivers can validate needed blocks without separate inter-GPU barriers. On a server with eight NVIDIA B300 GPUs, all-reduce latency fell by a median of 28.8% (up to 43.7%) compared with custom AR v2, and time per output token dropped 1.7-6.8% in end-to-end decoding.

entry.title: AtomicFaaS: Offloading Side-Effect Compensation to the Serverless Platform
entry.summary: AtomicFaaS: Offloading Side-Effect Compensation to the Serverless Platform arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes AtomicFaaS, an extension to serverless platforms that gives a function's external side effects semantic atomicity, even if the function fails or its instance crashes. It removes the need for developers to write compensation code. The system intercepts outbound calls, records their effects in a fault-tolerant log, and lets the platform compensate leaked effects outside the failed instance. Compared with a manually written saga, it eliminates compensation code, adds about 1 ms per intercepted call, and leaves no compensatable effects in any tested failure.

entry.title: Mechanism design for an incumbent seller facing a substitute-good rival
entry.summary: On Competing Sellers with Substitutable Goods arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies an incumbent seller who faces an entrant selling a substitute good. The incumbent commits to a possibly randomized mechanism before the competitor responds, and a unit-demand buyer observes both mechanisms and can interact with them in either order. The authors determine the incumbent's exact optimal revenue and characterize all mechanisms achieving it. They show that commitment and randomization let the incumbent earn strictly positive revenue even against an arbitrarily superior product, unlike posted-price competition.

entry.title: Tutorial on distributed consensus, optimization, and learning under communication limits
entry.summary: Distributed Consensus, Optimization, and Learning under Communication Constraints arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This tutorial article explains how networked nodes reach agreement and jointly optimize a shared objective through local exchanges. It starts from the fundamentals of consensus averaging and distributed optimization and examines how network connectivity, information flow, and communication uncertainty affect cooperation and performance. Building on these insights, it discusses design principles for communication-constrained distributed learning across network topologies and reviews communication-efficient approaches, particularly for wireless networks.

entry.title: Energy-accumulating backscatter communication with retransmission under imperfect feedback detection
entry.summary: Energy-Accumulate-Then-Act Backscatter Communications With Retransmission Under Imperfect Feedback Detection arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a threshold-triggered backscatter communication system that accumulates harvested energy across transmission blocks and supports retransmission when feedback detection is imperfect. The device switches among energy harvesting, initial transmission, and retransmission modes based on its stored energy and decoded feedback. The authors derive the average age of information and the packet loss rate caused by imperfect feedback detection using an embedded Markov chain. Simulations show that retransmission reduces packet loss but may either improve or worsen age of information depending on packet-generation energy, data rate, and feedback power.

entry.title: Efficient Byzantine agreement without threshold signatures
entry.summary: Optimal Subcubic Byzantine Agreement with Plain PKI arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies Byzantine Agreement, where n parties must agree on a common value despite t malicious parties, in the synchronous setting. Previously, optimal-resiliency protocols (t < n/2) relied on threshold signatures, while protocols using regular signatures had cubic complexity. The authors present a deterministic protocol that uses plain PKI, achieves optimal resiliency t < n/2, has sub-cubic bit complexity, and runs in O(n) rounds.

entry.title: OSD-JSCC: Neural Joint Source-Channel Coding Using One-Step Diffusion for Image Transmission
entry.summary: OSD-JSCC: Neural Joint Source-Channel Coding with One-Step Diffusion arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes OSD-JSCC, an SNR-adaptive framework that transmits pretrained VAE latents through a neural joint source-channel codec. It uses a single diffusion step to refine reconstructions, improving visual quality over blurry distortion-optimized outputs. On Kodak and CLIC2020, it reduces LPIPS by about 43% and 53% relative to existing diffusion-based JSCC baselines, with decoding latency reduced by up to 50.6 times.

entry.title: Performance portability of out-of-kernel GPU optimizations, illustrated with molecular docking
entry.summary: Performance Portability of Out-of-Kernel Optimizations on GPUs: A Molecular Docking Case Study arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to keep GPU performance portable for irregular scientific workloads, using molecular docking as a case study. The authors propose an out-of-kernel tuning method that treats batching policy, worker concurrency, and per-worker memory allocation as explicit parameters, using explicit resource bounds instead of occupancy-driven choices. The method is implemented in the muDock mini-app and evaluated on NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs with CUDA, HIP, and SYCL. The fully tuned approach improves end-to-end throughput on all tested configurations, with an average speedup of 1.53x over the baseline.

entry.title: Fano's inequality and channel capacity for individual sequences
entry.summary: Fano's Inequality and Channel Capacity in the Individual-Sequence Regime arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper derives an individual-sequence version of Fano's inequality, replacing entropy with Lempel-Ziv complexity and error probability with empirical error frequency. It yields a converse: reliable communication is possible only at rates not exceeding the individual-sequence LZ channel capacity. The authors also prove a matching achievability result for symbol-wise invertible channels, including group-additive channels, using a universal decoder that needs no channel knowledge or feedback.

entry.title: CARE-FL: Federated Fine-Tuning of Multimodal LLMs on Resource-Limited Edge Networks
entry.summary: CARE-FL: Federated Fine-Tuning of Multimodal LLMs in Resource-Constrained Edge Networks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes CARE-FL, a constraint-aware online client-selection framework for federated LoRA fine-tuning of multimodal large language models. It models client participation as a sequential decision process, using Q-value decomposition and a modified Double Deep Q-Learning scheme to estimate long-term client utility under per-round latency and bandwidth constraints. Experiments on the CrisisMMD disaster-response task in emulated heterogeneous wireless edge environments report higher and more stable test accuracy than the compared baselines while satisfying those constraints.

entry.title: An exact link between transport cost and information geometry for adaptive discretization of distributions
entry.summary: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies how discretizing a continuous probability distribution affects transport cost and its relation to information geometry. The authors introduce a local-map scheme that moves the probability mass in each cell to that cell's own probability-weighted centroid. This makes the transport cost of each cell expressible through the covariance of its conditional distribution and the Fisher metric, and it establishes an exact correspondence with the expected Fisher-induced quadratic form. The result holds for finite-scale cells, without uniform cell geometry, full coverage, or an infinitesimal-scale limit.

entry.title: vExpert: Virtualized Expert Storage for Adaptive Load Balancing in Distributed MoE Inference
entry.summary: vExpert: Virtualizing Expert Storage for Adaptive Load Balancing in Distributed MoE Inference arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Distributed deployment of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models suffers severe load imbalance because static expert placement conflicts with dynamic routing. The paper proposes vExpert, which shifts host DRAM offloading from partial residency to full redundancy by virtualizing expert storage and dynamically mapping physical experts to virtual slots at runtime. It introduces a performance model that jointly captures H2D latency, PCIe contention, and load imbalance, along with a disaggregated manager that reduces memory overhead in multi-process settings. On DeepSeek-V3.1 in an 8-node H100 cluster, vExpert improves load balance ratio by up to 55% and achieves a 1.2× end-to-end speedup.

entry.title: Bottlenecks in LLM-based lossless compression: what can be removed and what must be traded
entry.summary: The Invocation Bottleneck in LLM-Based Lossless Compression: What Can Be Removed and What Must Be Traded arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines why LLM-based lossless text compressors are slow to decompress, attributing the delay to execution redundancy and sequential dependency. The authors remove execution redundancy with a GPU-resident pipeline using batch-invariant kernels, which keeps half-precision block-parallel encoding lossless and speeds up arithmetic coding by up to 5.8x in encoding and 3.0x in decoding without changing the compression rate. They then study two ways to trade away sequential dependency, speculative dual-model coding and multi-token single-model coding, and characterize the compression cost of predicting several tokens from a shared prefix.

entry.title: Hotplug Coded Caching: Embedding YMA and Interference Elimination Schemes via Reed–Muller Codes
entry.summary: Hotplug Coded Caching: Embedding the YMA and Interference Elimination Schemes via Reed--Muller Codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the hotplug coded caching model, where K users fill caches of size M from N files, but only an unknown subset of A<K users is active during delivery. The authors show that every point of the YMA scheme for a classical A-user system is achievable in the hotplug model for all K≥A, using projective Reed–Muller codes. By an existence argument, classical schemes with linear compressions of the Maddah-Ali–Niesen cache, including Tian and Chen's interference elimination schemes, can also be embedded over a sufficiently large field.

entry.title: Energy-efficient reinforcement learning for large language models
entry.summary: Energy-Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents EE-RL, an online controller that selects separate GPU clock frequencies for the generation and training stages of reinforcement learning for language models. It keeps the most energy-efficient setting that meets a throughput threshold, and monitors and adjusts frequencies as the workload changes. Experiments on H100 and GB200 GPUs show that EE-RL reduces GPU energy per valid training token by up to 16.9% at a modest throughput cost.

entry.title: Iterated elimination of dominated mixed strategies: comparing rounds of two procedures
entry.summary: Iterated Elimination of Dominated Mixed Strategies arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper compares two iterated dominance procedures, one eliminating mixed strategies and the other eliminating pure strategies. In compact and continuous games, the mixed-strategy procedure terminates at most one round after the pure-strategy procedure, and this bound is tight. The paper also gives two characterizations of the mixed-strategy procedure, equivalent round by round, which check for improvements only against opponents' pure strategies.

entry.title: Runway Characters: Serving a 57B Video Diffusion Transformer for Real-Time Conversation
entry.summary: Runway Characters: Serving a 57B Video Diffusion Transformer for Real-Time Conversation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper describes Runway Characters, a system that generates conversational video characters in real time for one user at a time. It serves an approximately 57B-parameter autoregressive video diffusion transformer at 704×1088 and 24 fps on four H100 GPUs, working with a voice agent. The authors reduce per-step cost by moving repeated cache work to write time and fusing communication with FP8 GEMM, cutting the diffusion step from 240.9 to 159.3 ms, and to 147.4 ms with the fused kernel.

entry.title: Easy multi-precision speedups through vectorized code
entry.summary: Easy Multi-Precision Acceleration via Vectorization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether simple vectorized coding techniques in high-level languages can deliver strong performance across many numeric precisions and hardware generations. The authors test memory bandwidth, real and complex matrix multiplication, and FFT-based 2D convolution on systems spanning nearly a decade. They report that near-peak hardware performance is readily reachable from high-level environments, and that algorithms trading compute intensity for memory intensity show significant potential.

entry.title: When Burning Money Helps Traders in Bilateral Trade
entry.summary: The Power and Limits of Money Burning in Bilateral Trade arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies whether a mechanism that burns money, charging the buyer more than the seller receives so the difference is lost to both, can benefit traders in bilateral trade with private values. Previously, money burning was known to only hurt traders under Bayesian and deterministic dominant-strategy incentive-compatible mechanisms. The authors show that once dominant-strategy mechanisms can randomize, money burning can significantly benefit both traders by arbitrarily large amounts. However, these randomized money-burning mechanisms still cannot guarantee any constant fraction of the first-best gains from trade.

entry.title: A mechanism for collective foraging: percolating recruitment cascades coupled to a maximum-entropy field
entry.summary: A self-organizing mechanism for collective foraging: recruitment cascades couple Levy search to a clustered maximum-entropy resource field arXiv · Oct 18, 2026This paper proposes a collective foraging model in which an agent that finds a resource recruits others through a linear-threshold cascade, and its movement rewires the communication network, producing a self-limiting cycle of aggregation and release. The authors report that recruitment to discoveries, marginal-value patch leaving, and Lévy search with local exploitation emerge together without tuning. Gains reach up to 7.6 times the harvest of solitary search when resources are sparse and clustered.

entry.title: Tighter Approximation and Competition Bounds for Simple Auctions
entry.summary: A Bulow-Klemperer Theorem for Bundling and Improved Approximation Bounds for Simple Auctions arXiv · Oct 18, 2026The paper studies simple auctions for one additive buyer whose values for several items are independent. For regular items, it proves that grand-bundle second-price revenue with two bidders lies between optimal revenue and twice bundling revenue, which is tight and answers an open question. For general independent items, it improves the approximation factor from 6 and 5.2 to 2.645, and raises the known lower bound from 2 to 2.11. ★★★★★ Notable: For independent regular items the authors show REV≤BSPA₂≤2BREV, answering an open question of Beyhaghi et al.; for general items they report a 2.645 approximation and a lower bound above 2.11.

entry.title: Pareto-optimal Scheduling with Predictions: a paper on single-machine job scheduling that balances trust in predictions against worst-case performance.
entry.summary: Pareto-optimal Non-Clairvoyant Scheduling with Predictions arXiv · Oct 23, 2026The paper studies preemptive single-machine scheduling where a prediction of job order or sizes is available, with the goal of minimizing total completion time. The authors exactly determine the best possible trade-off between consistency and robustness for deterministic algorithms. They give a greedy algorithm achieving this trade-off and prove a matching lower bound. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize the optimal consistency-robustness tradeoff for deterministic algorithms, reporting 1+ε consistency with ε^{-1/2}+1/6+O(√ε) robustness, versus prior Θ(1/ε).

entry.title: Balanced Fair Division and Generalized Kneser Graphs
entry.summary: Balanced Fair Division and Generalized Kneser Graphs arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies allocating indivisible goods to two prescribed nonempty groups whose members have arbitrary monotone valuations. It guarantees balanced envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) for up to five agents and up to two goods (EF2) for up to nine agents. These results follow from chromatic bounds for generalized Kneser graphs KG(2n,n,r). The authors also resolve a conjecture of Jafari and Alipour and improve known bounds on the chromatic number for r=3. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report EF1 guarantees for up to five agents and EF2 for up to nine in balanced division of indivisible goods, and state that the chromatic number of generalized Kneser graph KG(2n,n,2) is

entry.title: Near-MMS fair allocations when few extra agents are present
entry.summary: Almost-MMS allocations with small agent redundancy arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies fair allocation of indivisible goods, asking whether a subset of n agents among more agents can each receive at least a fixed fraction of their n-maximin share (MMS). The authors show that when agent redundancy is positive, this fraction approaches 1 as n grows. This also holds without redundancy when the number of goods is at most (2−c)n. Adapting their techniques, they improve a result of Ezra and Garbuz, showing that without redundancy, n−O(log²n) agents can always receive their full MMS. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show that with agent redundancy the MMS fraction tends to 1 as n grows, yielding a corollary for m≤(2-c)n and improving Ezra and Garbuz's result.

entry.title: Fast Equilibrium Computation for the Colonel Blotto Game
entry.summary: Efficient Equilibrium Computation in Colonel Blotto Games arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies Colonel Blotto, a resource-allocation game where two players split budgets across battlefields and the higher allocation wins each battlefield's value. It gives a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme that computes an epsilon-Nash equilibrium in time polynomial in the input length and 1/epsilon. For sufficiently balanced budgets and battlefield values, it also computes exact equilibria in linear time. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for equilibria in Colonel Blotto games, plus linear-time exact equilibria for balanced cases.

entry.title: Tight Bound for Randomized Truthful Scheduling
entry.summary: Tight Analysis of Randomized Truthful Scheduling: An (m+1)/2 Lower Bound arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies randomized truthful mechanisms for minimizing makespan on unrelated machines. It proves a lower bound of (m+1)/2 on the approximation ratio for truthful-in-expectation mechanisms, determining the optimal ratio as m/2 plus a constant. It also raises the leading constant of the lower bound for universally truthful mechanisms from 3/2−√2 to 1/2, which together with a known upper bound settles that ratio up to lower-order terms. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove a (m+1)/2 lower bound for randomized truthful makespan scheduling, improving the leading constant from about 0.0858 to 1/2.

entry.title: Tight limits for fair-in-expectation job scheduling on machines
entry.summary: Sharp Bounds for Truthful-in-Expectation Scheduling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies randomized mechanisms that schedule indivisible jobs on n unrelated machines, where each selfish machine owner privately knows its job processing times. The mechanisms are truthful in expectation and aim to minimize the expected makespan. For n of at least 7, the authors prove the optimal approximation ratio is (n+1)/2, and they give a matching mechanism. For two machines the optimal ratio is about 1.505995705434, and for three machines it is 2. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a matching lower and upper bound of (n+1)/2 for n≥7 and exact constants for two and three machines, for truthful-in-expectation scheduling.

entry.title: Constant-factor fair-share guarantees for subadditive valuations
entry.summary: Toward Constant-Factor Maximin Share Guarantees for Subadditive Valuations arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies maximin share (MMS), a fairness measure for dividing indivisible goods among n agents. For general subadditive valuations, it improves the known guarantee from Ω(1/log log n) to Ω(1/log* n). It also introduces q-partitioning valuations, an intermediate class between subadditive and XOS, and proves constant guarantees when q/n has a positive lower bound. For XOS valuations, the universal guarantee rises from about 0.2353 to 0.3125. ★★★★ Notable: The authors improve the general subadditive MMS guarantee exponentially to Ω(1/log* n) and report constant guarantees for intermediate q-partitioning valuation classes.

entry.title: Computational Complexity of Continuous Contract Design over Polymatroids
entry.summary: The Complexity of Continuous Contract Design over Polymatroids arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies optimal contracts where an agent allocates continuous effort under polymatroid capacity constraints. Linear costs admit polynomial-time computation of an optimal contract, while for quadratic costs the agent's best response is computable but optimizing the principal's share is NP-hard. The authors show an optimal quadratic-cost contract always exists with a share at most 1/2, which yields approximation schemes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show NP-hardness and exponentially many breakpoints for quadratic-cost contracts over polymatroids, and prove a share of at most 1/2 suffices for approximation.

entry.title: Distributed graph computation that survives node crashes
entry.summary: Local Distributed Computation under Crash Failures arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies deterministic algorithms for locally checkable graph problems in the synchronous LOCAL model, where crashing nodes may send messages to only some neighbors. The authors introduce consistent neighborhoods, which let a fault-free T-round algorithm be simulated locally and remain correct on subgraphs. The paper gives upper and lower bounds on the number of rounds needed to build these views, and reports complexity results for LCL problems and sinkless orientation under crashes. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce consistent neighborhoods for crash-tolerant LOCAL simulation, reporting near-tight upper and lower bounds plus LCL complexity separations.

entry.title: Randomized fair allocation of chores with a few disposals, guaranteeing a near-maximin-share standard
entry.summary: Best-of-Many-Worlds MMS Allocation for Chores with Sublinear Disposals arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies randomized (lottery-based) allocations of indivisible chores under additive costs. It introduces MMS1, a fairness notion requiring each agent's bundle to meet the maximin share bound after removing at most one chore. The main result shows that every instance admits an ex-ante proportional lottery whose every allocation is MMS1, with all but o(n) agents satisfying MMS. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce MMS1 and report ex-ante proportional lotteries where nearly all agents get MMS, improving known chore-allocation fairness bounds.

entry.title: Logarithmic comparison queries for fair item allocation
entry.summary: Logarithmic Comparison-Query Complexity for EF1 Allocations arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies how many comparison queries are needed to find an allocation of indivisible items among n agents that is envy-free up to one item (EF1). Algorithms may only ask which of two bundles an agent prefers, never seeing numerical values. The authors give algorithms using O(log m) queries for every fixed n≥2, matching a known Ω(log m) lower bound. The results cover both chores with nonnegative costs and goods with nonnegative valuations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve an open question, giving O(log m) comparison-query EF1 algorithms for every fixed n≥2, matching the known lower bound.

entry.title: A paper showing self-stabilising approximate clock synchronisation needs linear time
entry.summary: Self-stabilising approximate clock synchronisation requires linear time arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies clock synchronisation in distributed systems where processes may start in arbitrary states and up to f processes may suffer non-transient faults. The authors prove that deterministic self-stabilising approximate clock synchronisation tasks require Ω(f) time to stabilise, giving the first non-trivial time lower bound for these tasks. The result shows that tolerating both transient and non-transient faults is costly even for approximate synchronisation. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the first nontrivial Ω(f) time lower bound for self-stabilising approximate clock synchronisation, using a topological argument.

entry.title: Lower bounds for adaptive relaxed locally decodable codes
entry.summary: Lower Bounds for Adaptive Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes via the Capped Horvitz--Thompson Estimator arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper proves a nearly optimal lower bound on the blocklength of general relaxed locally decodable codes (RLDCs), extending prior results to nonlinear encodings and adaptive decoders with two-sided error. It shows that any q-query RLDC must have blocklength n = k^{1+Ω(1/q)}, closely matching a known upper bound. The proof reduces the problem to estimating the output distribution of adaptive decoders, using a capped Horvitz–Thompson estimator with bounded discrete derivatives on the p-biased cube. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors extend RLDC lower bounds to nonlinear encodings and adaptive two-sided-error decoders, obtaining a nearly tight n=k^{1+Ω(1/q)} bound via a capped Horvitz–Thompson estimator.

entry.title: Distributed LTL Synthesis under Arbitrary Message Adversaries
entry.summary: Distributed LTL Synthesis under Arbitrary Message Adversaries arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how two processes communicating in rounds over unreliable links can be automatically given distributed programs that satisfy linear temporal logic specifications, even though at least one message is delivered each round. It shows that this synthesis is undecidable in general, even when messages carry complete causal histories. The authors characterize exactly which communication restrictions, modeled as message adversaries, make synthesis decidable. For omega-regular adversaries, synthesis is decidable if and only if the image of the adversary's histories in the unit interval is nowhere dense. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give a complete characterization of decidable distributed LTL synthesis under message adversaries, linking it topologically to repeated bounded-time consensus.

entry.title: Computational Difficulty of Exact Autobidding Equilibria
entry.summary: On the Complexity of Exact Autobidding Equilibria arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how hard it is to compute autobidding equilibria, which link advertisers' value multipliers or participation probabilities through aggregate budget and ROI constraints. It establishes the exact computational complexity of finding these equilibria in several canonical settings, including second-price ROI pacing and budget- or ROI-constrained generalized second-price sponsored shopping. It also analyzes the complexity of approximating the equilibrium control vector when the target accuracy is given as input. ★★★★ Notable: The authors establish FIXP-completeness of exact autobidding equilibrium computation across several canonical settings, a new complexity characterization relevant to computational economics.

entry.title: EvoCG: A self-evolving precision-control method that speeds up conjugate gradient solvers
entry.summary: EvoCG: Self-Evolving Precision Control for Faster Conjugate Gradient arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents EvoCG, a mixed-precision conjugate gradient solver that uses a reinforcement-learning policy to choose precision for each tile during iteration. It is supported by a Tile-CSC mixed-precision SpMV kernel and a low-overhead in-loop runtime. Tested on 47 SPD matrices, it reports geometric-mean speedups over several baseline solvers and a time-to-solution gain over an FP64 version at the cost of more iterations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors treat tile-wise precision as online RL control within CG iterations, co-designed with a mixed-precision SpMV; reported 1.9–7x geometric-mean speedups across 47 SPD matrices.

entry.title: Binary Huffman coding with unequal letter costs is NP-complete
entry.summary: Binary Huffman Coding with Unequal Letter Costs Is NP-Complete arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies optimal binary prefix coding when letters have unequal costs. The authors prove that deciding whether a binary prefix-free code with frequency-weighted cost at most a given threshold exists is NP-complete, even when the letter costs are consecutive positive integers (M, M+1) given as input. The proof uses two polynomial-time reductions starting from Planar Independent Set. The result implies that finding an optimal code is NP-hard. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove NP-completeness of binary Huffman coding with unequal letter costs, via two polynomial-time reductions from Planar Independent Set.

entry.title: Plotkin-optimal pure quantum LRCs with large minimum distances from NMDS codes
entry.summary: Plotkin-optimal pure quantum LRCs with large minimum distances from NMDS codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a general framework for building optimal pure quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) that reach a Plotkin-like bound, using Hermitian dual-containing near maximum-distance separable (NMDS) codes. It focuses on extended subcodes of generalized Reed-Solomon (ESGRS) codes, determining their localities by analyzing subset sum problems over finite fields. Using the algebraic structure of these codes, the authors construct four families of such qLRCs with large lengths and more flexible minimum distances than existing constructions.

entry.title: Computing Distortion in Social Choice
entry.summary: Computational Aspects of Distortion arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies the distortion framework in social choice theory, which measures the efficiency of randomized selection of an alternative based on agents' preferences. The authors present a linear-programming algorithm that computes the optimal randomized decision for a given instance, which is simpler and faster than prior methods. They also give a non-convex quadratic programming algorithm to compute the exact distortion of any randomized positional scoring rule.

entry.title: Parallel Python implementation of sparse nonlinear dynamics identification (SINDy) using Numba, OpenMP, threads and multiprocessing, tested on Lorenz and Rössler systems
entry.summary: Parallel Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics in Python: Task- and Data-Parallel SINDy with Numba, OpenMP, Threads and Multiprocessing for the Lorenz and Rössler Systems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents an open-source Python implementation of SINDy, a method that recovers interpretable governing equations from time-series data by sparse regression. The same loop-based kernels are compiled with Numba and run on a shared-memory multicore node through four interchangeable back ends: Numba prange, OpenMP via PyOMP, Python threads, and multiprocessing with shared memory. On the Lorenz and Rössler systems, all back ends recover the exact sparsity pattern, reach 14.8 to 20.3 speed-up on 24 cores, and cut total time to solution by up to 117 times relative to PySINDy.

entry.title: What Limits Serving Speed in Looped Language Models: Measurements and Optimizations Ranked by Exactness
entry.summary: What Sets the Serving Speed of Looped Language Models? Measurements and Optimizations Graded by Exactness arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper measures how fast two looped language models, Ouro and Huginn-0125, can be served in an open-source inference engine. Because these models reuse the same block of layers many times per token, per-layer overhead is paid on every loop. The authors rank their optimizations from bitwise-identical changes to those requiring an accuracy check, and report throughput gains alongside effects on GSM8K accuracy.

entry.title: A study of numerical bugs in GPU programs and automated detection
entry.summary: An Investigation on Numerical Bugs in GPU Programs Towards Automated Bug Detection arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper analyzes 397 real-world numerical bug samples from GitHub in GPU programs, identifying their root causes, symptoms, triggering input patterns, test oracles, and fixing strategies. The authors also present GPU-NBDetect, a preliminary tool that detects numerical bugs across six bug categories. It found 226 bugs in 186 mathematical functions across four libraries, and developers confirmed 60 of them.

entry.title: Computer-aided design and checking of cheat-proof facility placement on distance networks
entry.summary: Search and Verification for Strategyproof Facility Location on Metric Graphs arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to automatically design randomized facility location mechanisms on continuous metric graphs that are strategyproof, with the goal of minimizing total distance. The authors develop methods for computing upper and lower bounds on the best approximation ratio achievable by such mechanisms, and introduce finite representations called piecewise-linear attributions. Certified upper and lower bounds are computed on several metric graphs.

entry.title: Analysis of Serverless Workloads Across Function-as-a-Service Platforms
entry.summary: Characterizing Serverless Workloads: A Large-Scale Analysis of Function-as-a-Service Platforms arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper compares eight publicly available Function-as-a-Service workload traces from major cloud providers and a scientific computing platform. It characterizes invocation patterns, latency, cold start behavior, and resource utilization. The authors report that execution times have shortened, shifting bottlenecks toward platform scheduling and dependency management, and that concurrent long-lived containers are increasingly used. They also find resource over-provisioning and highly skewed user request volumes.

entry.title: Rank-metric intersecting codes: extending intersecting codes to the matrix rank metric
entry.summary: Rank-metric intersecting codes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Intersecting codes are codes in which any two nonzero codewords share a common nonzero coordinate. This paper extends the notion to the matrix rank-metric setting, defining the support of a matrix as its row space.
