entry.summary: Token-as-a-Utility: A Model-Agnostic Architecture for Metering and Provisioning AI Inference Services arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper presents Token-as-a-Utility, an architecture that combines inference metering, service-level-aware provisioning, and settlement between operators. Consumption is measured in Reference Inference Units (RIUs), and occupancy-indexed operator ratings recover shared serving costs. Measurements on three GPUs and trace-driven multi-tenant experiments show lower energy estimation error and reduced tenant mispricing compared with flat token counting.

entry.title: Removing Servers from State Machine Replication (Serverless SMR, S²MR)
entry.summary: Eliminating Servers in State Machine Replication arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper proposes Serverless State Machine Replication (S²MR), which stores both the materialized state and the durable total order of commands on disaggregated storage, with clients maintaining the materialized state rather than servers. The authors build AirDB, a transactional key-value store, on this design. According to the paper's evaluation, AirDB over S²MR is unaffected by server failures and bad client activity and spins up 10x to 45x faster from a cold start than etcd over Raft.

entry.title: Randomized consensus that survives mobile crashes via multiple leaders
entry.summary: Beyond Leaderless: Randomized Consensus Against Mobile Crashes arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper addresses consensus protocols that fail to terminate when an adversary can move between replicas and repeatedly crash one of them. It proposes Multi-Leader Fixed-View Simplex (ML-FVS), in which several leaders may each broadcast a proposal and replicas vote on the set of proposals they have seen. A hidden threshold beacon revealed after voting ranks the proposals. Under a constant crash budget and delayed Byzantine corruption, the authors obtain O(Δ) expected latency, and they evaluate the protocol under random delays and stochastic faults.

entry.title: Sub-terahertz LEO satellite links: does Doppler shift pose a major design challenge?
entry.summary: Sub Terahertz LEO Satellite Communication: Is Doppler Shift a Major Challenge? arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies how Doppler frequency shift affects sub-terahertz low Earth orbit satellite communication using OFDM transmission. The authors build an evaluation framework covering both Doppler-induced and other signal impairments, and compare three engineering approaches to handling Doppler shift. They find that ignoring Doppler substantially degrades performance, but a few low-complexity measures eliminate most negative effects. A single Doppler estimate over a 5-minute satellite pass may suffice to maintain high performance throughout the connection.

entry.title: AdapBench: Adaptive Early-Stopping and Prioritization for Faster Cloud CI/CD Microbenchmarking
entry.summary: AdapBench: Adaptive Early-Stopping and Prioritization for Efficient Microbenchmarking in Cloud-based CI/CD arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper presents AdapBench, an online scheduling system that shortens the run time of microbenchmark suites so that performance regressions in new software releases are caught sooner. It decides at runtime which benchmarks to prioritize and stops each one early once enough evidence accumulates to accept or reject a performance change. Evaluated on eight Java projects and four Go projects, it saves 42% of aggregate execution time on Java and 85% on Go at matched detection and false-positive rates, with negligible scheduling overhead.

entry.title: Binary two-deletion and two-insertion channels: which received words maximize input entropy
entry.summary: Maximal input entropy for binary two-deletion and two-insertion channels arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper determines which received binary words maximize input entropy under uniform transmission over two-deletion and two-insertion channels. For two deletions, the maximizers are exactly the two alternating words at every positive received length. For two insertions, the same holds from received length five onward, with all smaller cases and exact maximal values given.

entry.title: A study of ET-SoC-1 vector and parallel performance using a matrix multiplication benchmark
entry.summary: Investigating ET-SoC-1 Vector and Parallel Performance with sGEMM arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies the performance of the ET-SoC-1, a massively parallel RISC-V accelerator, using single-precision matrix multiplication (sGEMM) as the benchmark. Two device kernels are implemented and evaluated: a register-blocked SIMD baseline and a TensorFMA32 kernel that drives the same arithmetic datapath through a tensor sequencer. Since both kernels share the same arithmetic peak, the comparison isolates the effect of operand delivery. The results are compared against several CPUs and GPUs.

entry.title: Shared randomness for sampling random permutations in parallel rounds
entry.summary: Shared Randomness and Parallel Rounds in Permutation Sampling arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies how much shared randomness is needed to sample a uniform random permutation when outputs are produced in parallel rounds. Coordinates committed in the same round are independent given the full history and the current shared choice, and each shared choice is charged the logarithm of its conditional support size, summed along the worst execution path. The authors determine optimal total-variation error under various shared budgets and round densities, and give the optimal cost for exact sampling in Θ(n) rounds.

entry.title: Automatic GPU block-size tuning for large stencil codes built on the OPS framework
entry.summary: Autotuning GPU Thread Block Sizes for Large-Scale Stencil Applications Using the OPS DSL arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper presents an extension to OPS that automatically selects thread block (workgroup) shapes for each GPU kernel. It tests valid shapes during execution, records the fastest configuration per kernel, and replays these settings in later runs. Evaluated on structured-mesh applications across 3 NVIDIA and 2 AMD GPUs, the approach improved most measured cases over the default shape, with some solvers exceeding 1.5x speedup.

entry.title: Order-4 Latin cubes and 4320-point quaternionic constructions in R^16 (a math paper on kissing configurations in 16 dimensions)
entry.summary: Latin cubes of order 4 and 4320-point quaternionic constructions in ℝ¹⁶ arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper concerns kissing numbers in 16 dimensions, where the known lower bound of 4320 comes from a shell of the Barnes–Wall lattice. The authors describe the known 4320-point configurations via the quaternionic construction and generalize it to a family parameterized by three Latin cubes of order 4 and six permutations of a 3-element set. Computer-aided counting shows there are 4,072,728,621 isometry classes in this family.

entry.title: A density theorem for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes
entry.summary: A density theorem for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proves a fixed-characteristic density version of the Berger-Charpin conjecture for non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes. For each prime p, the set of lengths admitting such a non-standard code over some finite field of characteristic p has natural density zero. Consequently, for almost all lengths coprime to p, such codes have only permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius map. The proof relies on the classification by Feng, Hollmann, Li and Xiang, a normal form for their derivation constructions, and a theorem of Wiertelak on multiplicative orders.

entry.title: Closed-form Gaussian mixture representations for triangulated domains in d dimensions
entry.summary: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper derives a closed-form Gaussian mixture (GM) representation of a finite-volume region in Euclidean space from a simplicial triangulation. On each simplex, the uniform density is replaced by the Gaussian density minimizing the KL divergence, via information projection onto Gaussian densities. Using affine isomorphisms, KL properties, and a partition-of-unity argument, the authors establish a sharp, dimension-dependent but geometry-independent upper bound on the global KL divergence to the uniform density. Numerical examples illustrate the approach and its practical potential.

entry.title: The covering radius of the nine-variable first-order Reed-Muller code is 242
entry.summary: The covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code in nine variables is 242 arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proves that the covering radius of the binary first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242, equivalently that the maximum nonlinearity of a nine-variable Boolean function is 242. The proof combines a one-point rigidity theorem with spectral and computational exclusion of the two larger candidate nonlinearities. Together with a known construction attaining nonlinearity 242, these arguments establish the result. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the covering radius of RM(1,9) equals 242, combining a one-point rigidity theorem with spectral and computational exclusion of larger candidates.

entry.title: LADS: Lease-Aware Scheduling for Delivering Tool Results to Language Model Agents
entry.summary: LADS: Lease-Aware Delivery Scheduling of Tool Results for Language Model Agents arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Web agents complete multi-step online tasks through repeated browser actions and model calls, and the observations they receive shape later decisions. The paper presents LADS, a tool-result scheduler that combines cache-aware delivery with bounded prefix leases. Compared with first-in, first-out (FIFO) delivery, LADS reduces mean complete-workflow latency by 44.6% under bursty tool returns and by 42.4% on Web-derived burst replay.

entry.title: Noise stability on the hypercube at order 7/8: a study of how balanced Boolean functions keep their values steady under random noise.
entry.summary: Noise Stability on the Hypercube: Order 7/8 arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies the alpha-stability of balanced Boolean functions on the discrete hypercube, defined via the Boolean noise operator for exponents between 0 and 1. Using asymmetric Hellinger kernel estimates recently established by OpenAI, it proves that dictator functions minimize the 7/8-stability in every dimension and at every correlation, and are the only minimizers at interior correlations. It follows that dictators minimize alpha-stability for 7/8 to 1, maximize it for 1 to 2, and maximize one-sided Shannon entropy stability. The result resolves a conjecture of Li and Médard and strengthens the Courtade–Kumar conjecture in the balanced case. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report proving dictators minimize the 7/8-stability at all correlations, resolving a Li–Médard conjecture and strengthening Courtade–Kumar in the balanced setting.

entry.title: Low-PAPR rank-2 DFT-s-OFDM waveform for 6G uplink
entry.summary: Low-PAPR Rank-2 DFT-s-OFDM Waveform for 6G Uplink arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes Cyclic Layer Assignment with Shared-basis Synthesis (CLASS), a rank-2 DFT-spread OFDM waveform scheme for 6G uplink. Constellation symbols are exchanged between the two layers before DFT spreading, using cyclic assignment patterns that generate diverse candidates while reusing a small set of waveform components. With only six inverse DFTs, CLASS explores 16 assignments and reduces the 99th-percentile worst-layer PAPR by 1.41 dB versus fixed assignment, outperforming SLM and PTS under the same synthesis budget.

entry.title: Position-Robust NOMA Design for Pinching-Antenna Systems
entry.summary: Service-Area Robust NOMA for Pinching Antennas Systems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) for pinching-antenna systems, where small user movements strongly affect the channel. The designs optimize antenna placement and power splitting over bounded service areas so that the weak user remains decodable at the strong user. A worst-case design for quasi-static users and an ergodic design for codewords spanning representative positions are proposed. Numerical results show NOMA generally outperforms orthogonal multiple access with a shared placement, and in the ergodic regime can still outperform orthogonal access with per-user antenna reconfiguration.

entry.title: Interleaved tokens and two-pass decoding for semantic image transmission
entry.summary: Spatial Token Interleaving and Two-Pass BP Decoding for Semantic Image Transmission arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes a semantic error control coding scheme for image transmission. A vector-quantized tokenizer converts images into tokens carried in 5G NR LDPC code blocks, and a spatial interleaver ensures adjacent tokens are carried by different blocks. After a first belief propagation pass, the receiver fuses BP token probabilities with predictions from the Emu3-Gen autoregressive model and runs a second decoding pass. On Kodak24 at 0.15 dB SNR, the second pass removes 92% of residual token errors and interleaving cuts the final token error rate by 88%, with at least 1.2 dB PSNR gain over deep joint source-channel coding baselines at medium to high SNR.

entry.title: Cyclotomic polynomials whose irreducible factors over finite fields have three terms
entry.summary: Cyclotomic polynomials with trinomial irreducible factors over finite fields arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper classifies pairs (q,n), where q is a prime power and gcd(n,q)=1 with n>1, for which every irreducible factor of the cyclotomic polynomial Φ_n(x) over F_q has exactly three nonzero terms. The greatest common divisor of the positive support exponents yields a unique reduction by a power substitution. The paper gives the corresponding arithmetic conditions and explicit factorizations. ★★★★ Notable: The authors classify pairs (q,n) for which all irreducible factors of cyclotomic polynomials over finite fields are trinomials, via power substitution reduction.

entry.title: When Shards Fly: A Method for Fast, Memory-Efficient Weight Updates in Distributed RL
entry.summary: When Shards Fly: Cross-Tensor In-Flight Conversion for Low-Latency, Low-Memory Weight Updates in Disaggregated RL arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses the latency and GPU-memory overhead of synchronizing policy weights between training and rollout GPU pools in disaggregated LLM reinforcement learning. It presents ShardFly, which pairs a Planner that compiles cross-tensor transfer schedules with an Executor that fuses layout conversion, quantization, communication, and writes in one persistent kernel. On up to 32 H20 GPUs, ShardFly achieves 1.26 to 27.92 times faster complete BF16 weight updates than four baselines across five models. In end-to-end Qwen3-30B-A3B GRPO, it improves response-token throughput by 5.49 to 6.71% over veRL NCCL.

entry.title: Equal-weight prime-power fields for cyclotomic factors and MDS constacyclic codes
entry.summary: Equal Hamming Weights at Fixed Root Order and Applications to Constacyclic MDS Codes arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies, for a fixed integer n>1, which prime powers q coprime to n make all monic irreducible factors of the cyclotomic polynomial over F_q share the same coefficient Hamming weight. It gives a finite, computable classification using cyclotomic orbit coefficients. As an application, it shows that an MDS constacyclic code with an irreducible generator forces all irreducible polynomials of the same root order to have full support.

entry.title: Efficient edge-device sharing of radar detection models for CBRS
entry.summary: Communication-Efficient Model-Distributed Inference for CBRS Radar Detection at the Edge arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses detecting radar and LTE/5G signals coexisting in the CBRS 3550-3700 MHz band using spectrogram-based YOLO detectors on resource-limited edge devices. The authors propose CEDAR, which includes CEDAR-YOLO, a detector that removes multi-scale structures to reduce communication costs when splitting the model, and CEDAR-MDI, a framework that adds lightweight activation compressors and selects partitions to minimize pipeline bottlenecks. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano with over-the-air data, the detector cuts parameters by 35-57% and inference time by 16-33%, and the framework reaches up to 3.27 times single-device throughput while preserving detection quality.

entry.title: Proof that exact equilibrium computation in three second-price auction models is FIXP-complete
entry.summary: FIXP-Completeness in Second-Price Auctions arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper proves that computing exact equilibria is FIXP-complete in three second-price auction models: return-on-investment pacing with a multiplier cap of 1+δ, budget-constrained generalized second-price sponsored shopping, and budget-constrained throttling. The proofs rely on a FIXP-complete generalized-circuit problem built from clipped affine gates and a reciprocal gate. The results address open questions on the exact complexity of automated bidding. ★★★★ Notable: The authors introduce a generalized-circuit FIXP-complete basis and report FIXP-completeness for three second-price auction equilibrium problems in automated bidding.

entry.title: GPU megakernels: why residency can mislead
entry.summary: Understanding GPU Megakernels: Why Residency Can Mislead arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper rebuilds two LLM megakernels, ThunderKittens and VDCores, as separate kernels on an H100 GPU using their original operator code. It finds that CTA residency can misrepresent opportunities for useful overlap in both directions. Overlapping startup and operand loading with programmatic dependent launch cut ThunderKittens' decode-step latency by 5.7%. The authors argue that resource availability governs overlap and that GPUs should support earlier resource reuse across kernels.

entry.title: Radar sensing of fast, distant targets in overspread channels using Zak-OTFS and modular arithmetic
entry.summary: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper addresses aliasing in delay-Doppler (DD) modulation when the channel spread factor exceeds one, which is common in long-range mobility scenarios such as drones and satellites. The authors propose a two-frame design that combines DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods on the same bandwidth and frame size, and use modular arithmetic on wrapped peak positions to recover each target. They introduce two receivers, DS and DS-XC, with DS-XC including cross-pilot cancellation. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC detects 98% of targets, compared with 81% for the best baseline.

entry.title: Coded Computing for Dynamic Systems Using Cartesian Products
entry.summary: Dynamic Coded Distributed Computing with Joint File Placement and Reduce Function Reassignment arXiv · Sep 30, 2026Coded distributed computing reduces Shuffle communication bottlenecks through coded multicast, but existing schemes assume a fixed set of workers and do not adapt to arrivals and disconnections. This paper proposes a dynamic scheme that keeps surviving workers' caches and Reduce assignments while using storage from newly arriving clusters. File placement uses Cartesian products of cluster-wise placement delivery arrays, and a greedy algorithm reassigns abandoned Reduce functions. The authors derive the exact communication load for arbitrary feasible disconnections and show, under one-shot communication and uncoded placement, that the scheme is within a factor of two of the lower bound when new clusters arrive without disconnections, and within a factor of four otherwise.

entry.title: Undirected network coding enables faster external-memory integer sorting
entry.summary: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting arXiv · Oct 14, 2026The paper gives a finite counterexample showing that, in undirected networks, network coding and fractional routing can achieve different rate combinations, contrary to the multiple-unicast conjecture. Using the counterexample's linear structure, it proposes a deterministic external-memory integer sorting algorithm whose block-transfer count is asymptotically smaller than the classical comparison-sorting bound in some parameter ranges. The algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound are formally verified in Lean. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors give a finite counterexample to the multiple-unicast conjecture and use its linear structure to obtain a deterministic external-memory integer sort whose I/O bound is asymptotically smalle

entry.title: A counterexample disproving a conjecture on non-abelian groups in additive combinatorics
entry.summary: A Counterexample to the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa Conjecture arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper gives a counterexample to the non-abelian version of the Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture. The construction is based on an equivalent maximal-coupling entropy inequality, for which a counterexample can be found in a lower-dimensional group. The authors give an explicit cardinality counterexample in the fourteenth direct power of the dihedral group of order 8, D_4^{14}. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a explicit counterexample to the non-abelian Gyarmati-Matolcsi-Ruzsa conjecture, via maximal-coupling entropy, in D_4^14.

entry.title: Proof that the covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9) is exactly 242
entry.summary: The covering radius of RM(1,9) is precisely 242 arXiv · Oct 16, 2026This paper studies the covering radius of the first-order Reed-Muller code RM(1,9), a code of length 2^9. Its covering radius was previously known to lie between 242 and 244, and determining the exact value has been a long-standing open problem. The authors give a computer-assisted proof that it equals 242, using a classification of the 349 orbits of RM(3,9)/RM(2,9) under GL(9,2). The verification notebook and data are publicly available in a code repository. ★★★★ Notable: The authors resolve the long-open covering radius of RM(1,9) via a computer-assisted proof using orbit classification under GL(9,2).

entry.title: Decentralized Dynamic Stable Matching: Computing and Learting Optimal Stable Matchings Without Clocks or Direct Communication
entry.summary: Decentralized Dynamic Stable Matching arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies how players can decentrally compute the player-optimal stable matching when players arrive and depart unannounced, without a common clock or direct communication. For known preferences, it gives a deterministic polynomial-time self-calibrating protocol with improved cost bound O(t_*+K^2 log T). For unknown preferences, it presents a decentralized learning protocol with expected cost O(t_*+K^4 Δ_min^{-2} log T), and a lower bound shows the dependence on T and Δ_min is tight. ★★★★ Notable: Decentralized dynamic stable matching without clocks or communication; the authors report improving cost from O(T^{1-1/K}) to O(t*+K^2 log T) with a matching lower bound.

entry.title: Online budgeted allocation's competitive ratio is strictly below 1-1/e
entry.summary: The Competitive Ratio of Online Budgeted Allocation is Strictly Smaller than 1-1/e arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper refutes a well-known conjecture in online algorithms, which held that the randomized competitive ratio of online budgeted allocation is 1-1/e. The authors show that every randomized online algorithm has a competitive ratio at most 1-1/e-ε. Here ε is a small positive absolute constant. ★★★★ Notable: The authors refute the long-standing conjecture that the randomized competitive ratio of online budgeted allocation is 1-1/e, proving a strictly smaller upper bound.

entry.title: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Agent LLM Serving
entry.summary: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Agentic LLM Serving arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses memory pressure from key-value caches in large language model serving, which requires eviction when capacity runs short. It proposes keeping shared prefixes, evicting cache from the start of the remaining history, and retaining the cached suffix, and builds a system called Penelope around this idea. Implemented in SGLang and tested on three Qwen3 model sizes with real agent traces, it reduces mean time to first token by up to 60% and job completion time by up to 37% with a GPU-only cache. With a two-tier GPU-CPU cache, the reductions reach up to 76% and 60%.

entry.title: A new upper bound on the maximum size of binary constant weight codes A(19,6,8)
entry.summary: A new upper bound for A(19,6,8) arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies the maximum number of codewords A(19,6,8) in binary constant weight codes. The authors compute Polak's bound A_4(19,6,8), obtaining about 673.04001, and provide an exact rational certificate showing A(19,6,8) ≤ 673. This improves the bound of 693 listed in Brouwer's table. The certificate is checked by a separate program using exact rational arithmetic.

entry.title: Sampling Strings Across the Full Complexity Range
entry.summary: Beyond Typical Strings: Sampling the Complexity Landscape arXiv · Oct 30, 2026Uniform random sampling of binary strings mostly yields high-complexity strings, leaving low- and intermediate-complexity strings largely unexplored. The authors adapt the nested neutral set estimator (NNSE), a Monte Carlo rare-event method, to estimate the complexity distribution of fixed-length strings. They apply it to several complexity measures, including LZ76, LZ78, CTW, BDM and block entropy, and introduce uniform complexity weighting (UCW), which weights complexity levels equally rather than individual strings...

entry.title: Comments on Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity
entry.summary: Comments on "Multidimensional Costas Arrays and Their Periodicity" arXiv · Oct 26, 2026Rubio and Torres conjectured that multidimensional Costas arrays can keep the Costas property in every window of their periodic extension only when the order is a power of two set by the domain's dimension. This paper gives a four-dimensional periodic Costas array of order 6 with two-dimensional domain and image, disproving the conjecture. The verification reduces to 36 windows and was confirmed by computer and in the Lean proof assistant. The array also attains the pigeonhole bound that Rubio and Torres used for non-existence results, showing that bound is tight.

entry.title: Energy-efficient drone covert communication using metaheuristic optimization methods.
entry.summary: Energy-Efficient UAV Covert Communications via Metaheuristic Optimization arXiv · Oct 22, 2026This paper studies a drone-assisted covert communication system serving a legitimate receiver while multiple colluding wardens with imperfect location information are present. The authors jointly optimize the drone's three-dimensional trajectory and transmit power to maximize covert energy efficiency. To solve the resulting non-convex problem with robust covertness constraints, they propose Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization methods and compare them with a Block Coordinate Descent with Successive Convex Approximation benchmark. Numerical results show that the proposed methods improve covert energy efficiency while satisfying covertness constraints.

entry.title: Modifying LDPC Codes Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues
entry.summary: Applying Changes to LDPC Codes by Using 3-Induced Matchings and Eigenvalues arXiv · Oct 19, 2026The paper studies how to modify the Tanner graph of LDPC codes to reduce short cycles while keeping the graph bipartite and its degree sequences unchanged. It gives a necessary and sufficient condition for a 3-induced matching to exist in bipartite graphs with girth at least 6, which offers more choices for such changes. Among these changes, the authors select the one that best reduces the number of 6-cycles, and they use subgraph eigenvalues to find 3-induced matchings, with numerical results on when the existence condition is checked.

entry.title: The Pareto Secretary Problem: online selection of Pareto-optimal observations
entry.summary: The Pareto Secretary Problem arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies an online selection problem in which observations arrive one at a time from an i.i.d. sample, and the goal is to pick one that is Pareto-maximal, meaning no other observation is at least as good in every coordinate and strictly better in one. It determines the optimal failure-probability order for fixed dimensions, covering independent coordinates and fixed positive definite Gaussian covariances. It also reports results under arbitrary dependence, where optimal success can tend to about 0.58.

entry.title: Transfer principles for gradient-based learning from simple scalar games to large network zero-sum games
entry.summary: From Scalar Games to Unconstrained Network Zero-Sum Games: Transfer Principles for Gradient-Based Learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies a broad class of gradient-based learning rules in zero-sum games. It shows that if a rule converges on all scalar zero-sum games, it also converges on any network zero-sum game, under a step-size condition tied to the norm of the game operator. Finite-time rates also transfer mode by mode, so the worst-case network response equals the largest scalar rate. Thus, analyzing scalar games is enough to characterize convergence over the network class.

entry.title: Embodied Movable Antennas: Reconfiguring Wireless Channels Using a Physical Agent's Mechanical Redundancy
entry.summary: Embodied Movable Antennas arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper proposes embodied movable antennas (MAs), which change antenna position and orientation using the mechanical degrees of freedom already present in physical agents rather than dedicated actuators. The authors distinguish task-coupled and task-preserving modes and use a redundant robotic manipulator as an example, deriving an exact Fourier representation of the multipath channel. Numerical results show substantial communication gains from task-preserving motion.

entry.title: Capacity and the Four Subspace Problem: Distributed Linear Computation and Cross-Ratio
entry.summary: Capacity Meets the Four Subspace Problem: Distributed Linear Computation and the Cross-Ratio arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies a setting where several users each observe a fixed linear function of common data, and a server must recover another linear function with zero error from one message per user. It examines the smallest case, three users observing a, b, and a+b while the server wants a+λb, whose four functions form lines with cross-ratio λ. The capacity depends on λ and the prime subfield: it equals 2 for harmonic cross-ratios, 3/2 for λ outside the prime subfield, and lies in [3p/(2p-1), 2] for other prime-subfield values.

entry.title: Extremal character spectra of finite projective systems (a math paper on how many distinct values a point multiset's character function can take on flats)
entry.summary: Extremal character spectra of finite projective systems arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies finite spanning multisets of points in the projective space PG(k-1,q) and the character function of such multisets. Under a total-multiplicity budget, it examines the maximum number of distinct values the character function takes on codimension-r flats. The case r=k-1 is solved completely, including minimum-cost multiplicity profiles. For r=1, the known upper bounds on the minimum length of these systems are improved.

entry.title: Matching Workloads to Blackwell: Power-Resolved Benchmarks of NVIDIA B200 and B300 for HPC and AI
entry.summary: Matching Workloads to Blackwell: Power-Resolved Benchmarking of NVIDIA B200 and B300 across HPC and AI Workloads arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper benchmarks NVIDIA's B200 and B300 (Blackwell Ultra) GPUs on two separate eight-GPU clusters, covering computer-vision inference and training, Llama-3 LLM inference, and six production HPC codes. It finds that the B300 is not a uniform successor to the B200, trailing it by up to several times on some workloads such as convolutional inference and double-precision Quantum ESPRESSO. The authors use per-GPU power draw to explain the convolutional gap and provide workload-specific procurement guidance.

entry.title: Approximate-support Donoho–Stark uncertainty principles for k-Hadamard operators
entry.summary: On approximate support versions of Donoho--Stark uncertainty principles for k-Hadamard operators arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies Donoho–Stark type uncertainty principles for k-Hadamard operators in finite dimensions, building on earlier work by Wigderson and Wigderson. It examines versions for approximate supports under ℓ^p norms. The authors show such results cannot extend to p>1 for matrices that are not special k-Hadamard. For special k-Hadamard operators, they prove the principle holds for 1≤p≤2, while showing it fails for p>2 even under the speciality condition.

entry.title: Layered reproducibility for HPC: a Feel++ and Ktirio Urban Buildings case study
entry.summary: Layered Reproducibility for High-Performance Computing Applications: The Feel++ and Ktirio Urban Buildings Case Study arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of reproducing high-performance computing work, caused by complex software stacks, heterogeneous hardware and costly validation. It proposes a layered strategy in which Feel++ provides a traceable software supply chain and Ktirio Urban Buildings (KUB) builds on it to manage versioned urban-building data, executable simulations and checksum-verifiable results. The approach moves reproducibility from late manual packaging to an artifact chain linking source commits, packages, containers, benchmark configurations, dataset versions, provenance records and generated results.

entry.title: Achievable rates and nearly lossless state transmission over a multi-access channel with causal state information
entry.summary: Rates and Nearly-Lossless State over a Multi-Access Channel with Causal State Information arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies transmitting both data and state over a memoryless state-dependent multi-access channel where encoders have causal state information. The state has a common component known to both encoders and two private components, each known to one encoder. Data must be recovered with arbitrarily small error probability, and the state sequence with arbitrarily small symbol-error rate. Assuming the capacity region without the state reconstruction constraint is nonempty, the authors derive the capacity region and show it is achievable using a Block-Markov scheme with binning and superposition coding.

entry.title: Batch universal prediction via conditional additive smoothing
entry.summary: Batch Universal Prediction via Conditional Additive Smoothing arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies batch regret, a measure of how well a predictor performs on a fresh test sequence after observing a batch of training sequences from the same unknown source. It analyzes conditional additive smoothing estimators for binary memoryless and first-order Markov sources, deriving their asymptotic batch regret. For memoryless sources, the optimal bias and resulting regret are shown to vary with the training batch size, extending Krichevsky's Poisson-based analysis. The authors also introduce a Rényi analogue of batch regret and identify the optimal predictors as conditional α-NML estimators.

entry.title: A deterministic commit rule on unstructured DAGs for optimistic replication.
entry.summary: A Deterministic Commitment Rule over Unstructured DAGs for Optimistic Replication arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses optimistic replication, where replicas execute client requests locally without synchronizing, so results may later be revised and consistency is only eventual. The authors propose a simple framework based on a causality directed acyclic graph, in which each replica represents the object state as a causally ordered set of client operations. The framework includes a deterministic commitment rule that adds virtually no message overhead beyond disseminating submitted operations.

entry.title: Where KV-Cache Error Matters in Looped Language Models: Ouro and Huginn Study
entry.summary: Where KV-Cache Error Lives in Looped Language Models: A Diagnostic Study of Ouro and Huginn arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies looped language models, which apply the same block of layers several times per token and keep a key/value cache for each loop. It examines where storage errors change the next-token distribution and how shared-weight errors accumulate, using Ouro-1.4B and Huginn-0125 with simulated quantization. Per unit of error, values carry most of the diagonal Fisher mass, but measured KL divergence is dominated by keys with larger quantization errors.

entry.title: Characterizations and MacWilliams-like identities for weakly regular bent partitions
entry.summary: Characterizations and MacWilliams-Like Identities of Weakly Regular Bent Partitions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies bent partitions in which every generated bent function is weakly regular. The authors characterize these partitions through the duals of component functions of vectorial bent functions and through two classes of linear codes. They show that for p not equal to 3, all generated bent functions are regular, and that for m equal to n/2 and n at least 4, such partitions come from spreads in most cases. The paper also establishes MacWilliams-like identities and gives nonexistence results for odd p.

entry.title: Feasibility of sensing with only the common stream in ZF-RSMA under imperfect CSIT
entry.summary: Feasibility of Common-Stream-Only Sensing in ZF-RSMA with Imperfect CSIT arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies whether the common stream of Rate-Splitting Multiple Access (RSMA) can be reused for sensing in integrated sensing and communication, avoiding dedicated probing signals. It analyzes the tradeoff in a zero-forcing downlink where the common power fraction must support common decoding, private decoding, and target detection under imperfect transmitter channel knowledge and imperfect successive interference cancellation. The authors prove the feasible set is either a closed interval or empty, and simulations identify regimes where common-stream-only sensing is viable.

entry.title: Shaping and finite-length analysis of quaternion-based Alamouti space-time codes
entry.summary: Shaping and Finite-Blocklength Analysis of Quaternionic Alamouti-Type Codes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies finite 2×2 Alamouti-type space-time codes built from maximal orders in definite quaternion algebras over the rationals. For primes q≡3 (mod 4), it proves that the Eisenstein case q=3 uniquely minimises finite quotient-alphabet energy at fixed minimum distance and alphabet size. It also derives a high-SNR expansion of information variance and mutual information for uniform inputs. Numerical comparisons support the results.

entry.title: Secure deterministic identification with feedback and sensing over state-dependent wiretap channels
entry.summary: Secure Deterministic Identification with Feedback and Sensing over State-Dependent Wiretap Channels arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies secure deterministic identification over state-dependent discrete memoryless wiretap channels with private noiseless feedback and a sensing distortion constraint. The encoder uses no local randomness and relies only on the identity and past feedback. The authors show that under certain conditions on the main channel, the secure identification capacity equals its non-secure feedback counterpart, without requiring positive classical wiretap secrecy capacity.

entry.title: A study of t-designs supported by self-orthogonal codes
entry.summary: On t-designs supported by self-orthogonal codes arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies self-orthogonal t-(v,k,λ) designs, where the codes generated by the designs are self-orthogonal and their minimum-weight-k codewords correspond to the blocks. Under the conditions t ≥ ⌊k/4⌋+1 ≥ 2 and t ≤ 11, the authors classify these designs. The result also yields a classification of self-orthogonal codes of minimum weight k whose minimum-weight codewords form a t-design under the same conditions.

entry.title: MemX: Memory-Aware Automatic Parallelism for Mixed-Vendor GPU Training
entry.summary: MemX: Memory-Aware Automatic Parallelism for Cross-Vendor Heterogeneous GPU Training arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents MemX, a system that automatically chooses parallelism settings for training large models on clusters mixing GPUs from different vendors. Unlike prior systems that focus mainly on iteration time, MemX jointly optimizes iteration time, peak memory usage, and memory balance across GPUs. Implemented on Megatron-LM, it achieves a 12.17% prediction error and searches 31,240 configurations in 26.5 seconds on two heterogeneous clusters.

entry.title: HiState: Hierarchical Prefix Caching for Hybrid LLM Serving in Agent Tasks
entry.summary: HiState: Hierarchical Prefix Cache Management for Hybrid LLM Serving in Agentic Workloads arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents HiState, a prefix cache management system for hybrid large language models that mix full attention and recurrent layers, targeting agent workloads. Agents often revisit earlier contexts, but existing systems may lack the recurrent checkpoints needed for those prefixes, forcing recomputation. HiState stores historical checkpoints on SSD while keeping key-value entries in fast memory, and uses adaptive checkpoint intervals and unified eviction to manage storage. Implemented on vLLM, it achieves up to 5.73x and 5.44x p99 TTFT speedups over vLLM-Marconi and SGLang-HiCache on real coding-agent traces.

entry.title: Kidney exchange allowing patients two willing donors
entry.summary: Kidney Exchange with Dual Donors arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies a kidney exchange model in which a patient may enroll with up to two proxy donors and use both when that leads to a compatible transplant. The authors formulate the resulting optimization problems under cycle and chain constraints and design approximation algorithms with provable guarantees. They also analyze strategic manipulation when patients hide a donor and show that randomization can achieve truthfulness. Experiments on synthetic graphs indicate that total transplants rise substantially even when only a small fraction of patients enroll two donors.

entry.title: RecIS: Unifying Sparse and Dense Computation to Speed Up Recommender Training
entry.summary: RecIS: Unifying Sparse and Dense Computation for Efficient Recommendation Training arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper presents RecIS, a GPU-centric framework for training recommender models that treats the full path from input features to dense computation as one optimization target. It combines adaptive fusion of feature transformations, a GPU Embedding engine with hash-based sharding and hierarchical communication, and a multistage pipeline that overlaps input preparation with dense computation. Evaluated on industrial recommender models, RecIS reaches up to 2.62 times the throughput of PICASSO and 1.15 times that of TorchRec, reducing step latency by up to 61.5% and 12.9%.

entry.title: LEO Satellite IoT Coverage Gaps and Retransmissions Analysis
entry.summary: LEO Constellation Analysis for Satellite IoT: An Analysis of Coverage Gaps and Retransmissions arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how intermittent visibility of low Earth orbit satellite constellations affects connecting Internet of Things devices, focusing on coverage gaps and retransmissions. The authors develop an ergodic framework for Walker Star constellations that computes gap rates, duration distributions, and retransmission success probabilities as spatial integrals over a two-dimensional torus. The framework closely matches a seven-day SGP4 simulation of the Iridium NEXT constellation, and shows that the number of orbital planes substantially affects packet-delivery probability with at most one retransmission.

entry.title: Beamfocusing in the far field with frequency diverse arrays for OFDM sensing and communication
entry.summary: Beamfocusing Beyond the Near Field: Frequency Diverse Arrays for OFDM-ISAC Systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines frequency diverse arrays (FDAs), which add frequency offsets across antenna elements so the beam can focus by range even in the far field. It compares FDA focusing with phased arrays and explains how FDAs coexist with OFDM. The authors find FDAs mainly benefit multiuser separation through location division multiple access. Numerical case studies show FDA-based location division multiple access achieves higher sum-rates than phased-array schemes for far-field users with small angular separation.

entry.title: A new sparse optimization algorithm using subspace Newton steps with thresholding
entry.summary: Sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding algorithm for sparse optimization problems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes a sparse descent direction based on the Newton direction within a low-dimensional subspace for sparse optimization problems. Combining this direction with hard thresholding and orthogonal projection, the authors develop an algorithm called SDSNT. They establish its global convergence under the restricted isometry property with δ_{3k} ≤ √(3/20) for the measurement matrix. Experiments on random sparse vector recovery and audio signal reconstruction show SDSNT performs comparably to several state-of-the-art methods, with better recovery at high sparsity and better efficiency at low sparsity.

entry.title: Porting a Fortran climate model to C++/Kokkos using an AI coding agent
entry.summary: Migrating a Legacy Scientific Application with an AI Coding Agent: NICAM from Fortran to Kokkos arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper describes using the AI coding agent Claude Code to migrate NICAM, an OpenACC-accelerated Fortran climate model, to C++/Kokkos. About 140,000 lines of Fortran were translated into 35,000 lines of C++/Kokkos, covering the dynamical core and seven physics packages. A 100-member ensemble comparison showed the port is statistically consistent with the original model. On GH200 and MI300A clusters, the application achieved speedups of 1.71 and 1.54 times, respectively.

entry.title: Sparse signal recovery via scaled-gradient hard thresholding
entry.summary: Scaled-Gradient Hard Thresholding Algorithms for Sparse Signal Recovery arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper introduces scaled-gradient hard thresholding (SGHT) and its pursuit variant SGHTP for recovering sparse signals. The methods scale the gradient componentwise, keeping large components and attenuating smaller ones, then apply hard thresholding iteratively. Under suitable restricted isometry conditions, the authors derive recovery error bounds that account for measurement noise and deviations from exact sparsity. Experiments on the tested ECG signals show SGHTP performs comparably to established pursuit methods.

entry.title: Truthful, admissible principal-agent testing when nuisance parameters are unknown
entry.summary: Truthful and Admissible Principal--Agent Testing with Nuisance Parameters arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies statistical contracts that reward experimenters based on evidence from costly studies, aiming to deter ineffective proposals and elicit honest parameter reports. Under risk neutrality and a fixed participation cost, it constructs menus of e-values so that null-type agents have no incentive to participate, alternative-type agents earn positive expected profit, and truthful reporting uniquely maximizes reward. For Gaussian observations, it separately treats agents who know both mean and variance and those who know only the mean.

entry.title: POST-MIMO: Partition-based semantic transmission of 3D point clouds over MIMO wireless links
entry.summary: POST-MIMO: Partition-Oriented Semantic Transmission for MIMO Point Cloud Delivery arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of wirelessly delivering 3D point clouds, which involve large data volumes and irregular geometry, over multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The proposed POST-MIMO framework splits a point cloud into spatially coherent blocks aligned with parallel MIMO streams, encodes them with a hierarchical encoder, and reconstructs them at the receiver with a progressive decoder. Experiments show better reconstruction quality and lower computational resource use than representative reference schemes in the considered MIMO setting.

entry.title: Falcons: Faster Lossy Compression with Higher Ratios for Parallel Scientific Computing
entry.summary: Falcons: Pushing the Speed-Ratio Limits of Lossy Compression for Parallel Scientific Applications arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents Falcons, an error-bounded lossy compressor designed for large-scale parallel scientific applications. It combines SIMD-vectorized memory-regularized interpolation, distribution-adaptive lossless coding, and optimizations for multiple parallelization schemes. On cutting-edge supercomputers, Falcons reportedly improves compression ratio by up to 29% and throughput by up to 255% over state-of-the-art compressors. In the WRF weather application workflow, it provides a 1.55x end-to-end speedup.

entry.title: ZenKO: A Guided Iterative Quantum-Classical Method for Molecular Electronic Structure
entry.summary: ZenKO: Guided and Iterative Quantum-Classical Method for Molecular Electronic Structure using Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper proposes ZenKO, a gradient-based iterative sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) method for computing molecular ground states with a hybrid quantum-classical approach. ZenKO splits configuration selection into discovery, validation, and refinement steps to enable targeted subspace expansion. Evaluations on H2O, H10, and N2 molecules show improved ground-state accuracy over prior iterative methods and significantly lower classical computational cost.

entry.title: On the Communication-Sensing Tradeoff in DMT-Optimal Space-time-Coded ISAC Systems
entry.summary: On the Communication-Sensing Tradeoff in DMT-Optimal Space-time-Coded ISAC Systems arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies the tradeoff between communication reliability and sensing performance in integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems that use DMT-optimal space-time codes. It proposes an analytical framework and a sensing diversity order metric for high-SNR sensing reliability. The authors show that Perfect codes eliminate sensing blind spots for all nonzero codewords, and they introduce a spatial precoding method that preserves optimality while shaping the transmit beampattern. Simulations show about 3 dB sensing-gain improvement over the unprecoded Perfect code for a narrow target angular region.

entry.title: When Heterogeneity Helps: GPU and WSE Complementarity in Systems
entry.summary: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems arXiv · Oct 29, 2026This paper studies unified systems that combine GPUs and wafer-scale engines (WSEs) for AI workloads. The two differ in compute, memory, and communication organization, which creates both architectural complementarity and extra overheads. The authors propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU-WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity. They also present an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level gains.

entry.title: Moving Antennas Keep Gradients Intact for Learning on Mobile Devices
entry.summary: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable-Antenna Compensation of Channel Aging in Over-the-Air Split Learning arXiv · Oct 16, 2026The paper studies over-the-air training in which a moving terminal rotates the backpropagated gradient. A movable antenna that keeps pace with the terminal can rotate it back without channel estimation. The authors give a speed law and a bias-jitter law, and simulations on 3GPP CDL-A channels report 98.58% accuracy versus 98.59% with ideal CSI.

entry.title: Study showing asynchronous session processes with nested session types are Turing complete
entry.summary: On the Expressiveness of Asynchronous Processes with Nested Session Types (Extended Version) arXiv · Oct 23, 2026This paper studies the expressiveness of Asynchronous Session Processes (ASP), the process model tied to Nested Session Types (NSTs), which can describe nested recursive protocols beyond traditional regular session types. The authors prove the model is Turing complete by encoding two-counter machines into typed processes. The encoding uses a state-aware representation of counters and instructions governed by NSTs. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove the asynchronous nested session process model is Turing complete by encoding two-counter machines into typed processes.

entry.title: Learning finite-memory binary sources: estimating the statistical rules of short-memory bit sequences from one long data stream.
entry.summary: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies how many samples are needed to estimate biased binary sources with finite memory from a single trajectory, a task relevant to entropy estimation in cryptography. It establishes sharp sample complexity bounds with matching upper and lower limits that do not depend on mixing time or spectral gap. The authors conclude that some published entropy-source validation trace lengths may be insufficient under these bounds. ★★★★ Notable: The authors give tight sample complexity bounds for finite-memory binary sources using de Bruijn chain hitting times and majorization, questioning existing entropy-source validation trace lengths.

entry.title: Computing functions from distributed databases while protecting private attributes
entry.summary: Privacy-Constrained Function Computation in Distributed Databases arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper studies distributed databases holding both private and public attributes, where a user computes a function of public attributes and side information by querying and downloading responses. It analyzes the trade-off among download cost, leakage about private attributes, and distortion, characterized as a capacity region. Results cover single-database and distributed settings for discrete and Gaussian sources, as well as lossless computation.

entry.title: Characterizing how fine-tuning large language models runs on serverless GPU clusters
entry.summary: LLM Fine-Tuning Workloads: Characterization, Challenges, and Opportunities for Serverless AI arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper studies how fine-tuning jobs for large language models behave on clusters with different GPU types, using IBM's LLMFineTuningBench dataset of 30,920 experiments. It quantifies throughput, scaling, failure rates, and optimization potential across setups from 1 to 32 GPUs. The authors find that whether a job succeeds depends on workload properties, with failure ratios rising as batch size grows.

entry.title: Prefix Keys and Values Matter Late: RIPE Caching for Looped Models
entry.summary: Recency Is the Wrong Axis: A Negative Result on Windowed Deepest-Plane KV Caching in Looped Language Models arXiv · Oct 26, 2026This paper studies the key-value cache of looped language models, which run the same layer block several times per token. It finds that later loops are far more sensitive to prefix keys and values than earlier ones. The authors propose RIPE, which stores only the deepest cache plane except for a window of recent positions kept at full depth. Experiments on Huginn and Raven-Llama report self-speculative decoding speed-ups and memory savings.
